body:
A habit is an atomic routine that is easy to do
but has life-changing power. Good habits lead to
small improvements on a daily basis. Over time,
these tiny improvements can make a huge
difference in our lives. If you are seeking to build
and maintain good habits for a better life, here are
some valuable tips ⓐto guide you.
[What to Change]
Give Yourself a New Identity
You might find it (A)[easy / challenging] to develop
and ⓑmaintaining good habits for more than a few
days. This often happens when people focus on
ⓒchange external outcomes or behaviors rather than
on where they originate from — their inner identity.
Behavior change consists of three layers. The
outermost layer is outcome — ⓓwhat you achieve.
The middle layer is process — what you do. The
deepest and most (B)[fundamental / superficial]
layer is identity — what you believe or who you are.
While changes in all three layers ⓔis useful in their
own way, the key to lasting success lies in the
direction of change. True behavior change occurs
when there is a shift in your identity from (C)[within
/ outside]. If your new habit is not in harmony with
your identity, it is unlikely ⓕto last.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: easy fundamentalwithin
challenging superficialoutside
challenging fundamentalwithin
easy superficialwithin
challenging fundamentaloutside
solution: (A) 뒤에서 사람들이 좋은 습관을 유지하지 못하는 이유를 설 명하며 그 원인을 파고드는 흐름이 이어지므로, 좋은 습관을 며칠 넘게 기르고 유지하는 일은 쉬운 것이 아니라 어렵다고 해야 자연스럽다. 따라서 '어려운'이라는 뜻의 challenging이 알 맞다. easy는 '쉬운'이라는 뜻이다. (B) 세 층은 겉으로 드러나는 결과에서 점점 더 근본적인 층으 로 들어가는 구조로 설명되며, 정체성은 가장 안쪽 층으로 제 시된다. 뒤에 이어지는 most와 어울려 가장 근본적임을 나타 내야 하므로 '근본적인'이라는 뜻의 fundamental이 알맞다. superficial은 '피상적인'이라는 뜻이다. (C) 진정한 변화가 겉이 아니라 내면의 정체성이 바뀔 때 일어난 다고 보며, 바로 뒤에서도 습관이 정체성과 조화를 이뤄야 한다 고 말한다. 변화가 안에서 비롯된다는 흐름이므로 '내부로부터'를 뜻하는 within이 알맞다. outside는 '바깥에서'라는 뜻이다.

body:
Behavior change consists of three layers. The
outermost layer is outcome — what you (A)[want /
achieve]. The middle layer is process — what you
(B)[avoid / do]. The deepest and most fundamental
layer is identity — what you believe or who you are.
While changes in all three layers are useful in their
own way, the key to lasting success lies in the
direction of change. True behavior change occurs
when there is a shift in your identity from within. If
your new habit is not in harmony with your identity,
it is (C)[likely / unlikely] to last.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)          (B)        (C)
choices: wantdo      likely
achieveavoidunlikely
achievedounlikely
wantdolikely
achieveavoidlikely
solution: (A) 가장 바깥층인 '결과(outcome)'를 규정하는 자리로, 결과는 바라는 것이 아니라 실제로 이루어 낸 것을 가리킨다. 뒤의 process, identity의 정의와 나란히 놓이므로 (A)에는 '성취하다' 라는 뜻의 achieve가 알맞다. (B) 중간층인 '과정(process)'은 당신이 실제로 행하는 것을 뜻 하므로, (B)에는 '하다'라는 뜻의 do가 알맞다. (C) 진정한 변화는 내면의 정체성이 바뀔 때 일어나며 지속의 핵심이 정체성에 있다고 했으므로, 새 습관이 정체성과 조화를 이루지 않으면 오래가기 어렵다. 따라서 (C)에는 '~할 것 같지 않은'이라는 뜻의 unlikely가 알맞다.

body:
[How to Change]
Make Your Habit an Automatic Loop
After defining your desired identity, you will want
to (A)[integrate / separate] new habits into your
daily routines. It is worth noting here that any
lasting habits take as (B)[little / much] effort as
possible. To make habits take effect almost
automatically, we need to understand the concept
of the habit loop, which consists of four steps: cue,
craving, response, and reward. The more smoothly
this loop operates, the more easily the habit is
performed. The following four laws offer
(C)[theoretical / practical] guidance for each step.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: integratemuchpractical
integratemuchtheoretical
separatelittlepractical
separatelittletheoretical
integratelittlepractical
solution: (A) 되고 싶은 정체성을 정한 뒤 새로운 습관을 하루 일과에 자리 잡게 하려는 맥락이므로, 새 습관을 일과에서 떼어 내는 것이 아니라 일과 안으로 들여와야 한다. 따라서 '통합하다'라 는 뜻의 integrate가 알맞다. separate는 '분리하다'라는 뜻이다. (B) 뒤에서 습관이 거의 자동으로 시행되게 만드는 방법을 설 명하는데, 자동으로 이어지는 습관은 많은 노력이 아니라 가능 한 한 적은 노력이 드는 것이다. 따라서 '적은'이라는 뜻의 little이 알맞다. much는 '많은'이라는 뜻이다. (C) 뒤에 이어지는 네 가지 법칙은 각 단계에서 실제로 무엇을 하 면 되는지 알려 주는 구체적 지침이다. 따라서 '실용적인'이라는 뜻의 practical이 알맞다. theoretical은 '이론적인'이라는 뜻이다.

(B)[what / that] all your workout equipment is readily
available while keeping distractions away. Another
approach is the two-minute rule. When you start a
new habit, it should take less than two minutes to

on the floor.” This strategy is powerful because once

body:
Hello, everyone. Today we’ll discuss how to
effectively set goals using SMART strategies. SMART
stands for “specific, measurable, achievable, relevant,
and time-bound.” When setting a goal, it’s
important to be specific about what you want to
achieve. And make your goal measurable so you
can check your progress. Your goal should also be
realistically possible to achieve and relevant to your
life. Lastly, set a time limit to achieve it. For
example, if you used to say, “I want better grades,”
now say, “I aim to raise my math grade from a B
to an A by the end of the semester.” Use these
SMART strategies to set goals from now on. Thank
you.

위 담화의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the importance of improving school grades
how to manage your time wisely during a semester
the benefits of setting highly challenging goals
why many people fail to achieve the goals theyset
five key guidelines for setting goals more effectively
solution: 화자는 목표를 세울 때 구체적이고, 측정 가능하며, 현실적으로 달성 가능하고, 자신의 삶과 관련이 있으며, 기한을 정해야 한 다는 다섯 가지 기준을 차례로 설명하고 이를 적용한 예시를 제시하며 SMART 전략을 활용하라고 권한다. 따라서 주제로는 ❺ ‘목표를 더 효과적으로 세우기 위한 다섯 가지 핵심 지침’이 가장 적절하다.

[What to Change]
Give Yourself a New Identity
ⓐ당신은 며칠 이상 좋은 습관을 기르고 유지하는 것
이 어렵다고 생각할 수도 있다. This often happens
when people focus on changing external outcomes
or behaviors rather than on where they originate
from — their inner identity.
Behavior change consists of three layers. The
outermost layer is outcome — what you achieve. The
middle layer is process — what you do. The deepest
and most fundamental layer is identity — what you
believe or who you are. While changes in all three
layers are useful in their own way, the key to lasting
success lies in the direction of change. True
behavior change occurs when there is a shift in your
identity from within. If your new habit is not in
harmony with your identity, it is unlikely to last.
You can work on changing your identity through
two steps. First, keep asking yourself, “What kind of
person do I want to become?” Once you have an
idea of the kind of person you want to be, start
reinforcing that identity through your actions.
Specifically, repeat the action that kind of person
would choose to do, and over time, you will
naturally become such a person. For example, if you
want to start exercising daily, think of yourself as
an energetic and motivated person who cares about
his or her health. Then try to do the routines that
such a person would naturally do. Repeating these
routines will gradually lead you to become that
kind of person.

Lasting behavior change begins with a shift from
external outcomes to (A)______________, which should then be strengthened through
(B)______________ that reflect the person one wants
to become.
(A)　　　　　　　　　(B)
choices: desired identityimmediate rewards
external behaviorrepeated actions
inner identityconsistent actions
short-term resultsdaily routines
process goalscareful planning

W: We often hear that self-care is important, but
what is it exactly and how can we do it?
[What is self-care?]
Lisa: I think self-care is loving yourself and making
sure that you’re okay physically and mentally.
Jake: I see self-care as a battery recharge.
Nari: Self-care is looking after yourself and checking
whether you can continue doing your daily
routine.
[Why is self-care important?]
Lisa: Self-care is important because it prevents
burnout and helps you manage your stress.
Jake: Through self-care, you can restore your energy
so that you can fully enjoy your life.
Nari: Self-care helps you improve and make better
decisions.
[What can you do in terms of self-care?]
Lisa: There are many different things you can do,
so it’s important to figure out what works for
you. As for me, I treat myself to delicious
food.
Jake: Being social is a big thing for me. When I
hang out with my family or friends, I feel
re-energized.
Nari: I like to watch cat videos. It gives me a sense
of healing. I strongly recommend it.

위 대화의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the meaning, importance, and personal practicesof self-care
effective ways to manage stress and preventburnout
the value of taking time to recharge and relax
how to build healthy habits for a better daily life
the link between self-care and long-term productivity

body:
What is rewarded is repeated. When a behavior feels rewarding and satisfying, people are likely to repeat it. To maintain a new habit, it is important to experience a sense of immediate accomplishment, even in small ways. In fact, simply knowing that you are making progress is a quick and powerful motivating reward in itself. One effective method of keeping track of your progress is to use a habit tracker. This tool lets you use a formula like “After I [NEW HABIT], I will [TRACK MY HABIT].” For example, you can write “After I finish my daily workout, I’ll record it in my workout journal.” This provides you with moments of satisfaction, which helps you stick to your new habit.

Reward Others, Not Yourself, to Build Better Habits

body:
Hello, everyone. Today we’ll discuss how to
effectively set goals using SMART strategies. SMART
stands for “specific, measurable, achievable, relevant,
and time-bound.” When setting a goal, it’s
important to be specific about what you want to
achieve. And make your goal measurable so you
can check your progress. Your goal should also be
realistically possible to achieve and relevant to your
life. Lastly, set a time limit to achieve it. For
example, if you used to say, “I want better grades,”
now say, “I aim to raise my math grade from a B
to an A by the end of the semester.” Use these
SMART strategies to set goals from now on. Thank
you.

위 담화의 SMART에 대한 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Keep your goal broad rather than clearly definingwhat you want to achieve.
Frame your goal in a way that lets you trackhow far you have come.
Choose a goal that you can realistically reach.

body:
ⓐA habit is an atomic routine what is easy to do
but has life-changing power. Good habits lead to
small improvements on a daily basis. Over time,
these tiny improvements can make a huge
difference in our lives. If you are seeking to build
and maintain good habits for a better life, here are
some valuable tips to guide you.
ⓑYou might find that challenging to develop and
maintain good habits for more than a few days.
This often happens when people focus on changing
external outcomes or behaviors rather than on
where they originate from — their inner identity.
Behavior change consists of three layers. The
outermost layer is outcome — what you achieve. The
middle layer is process — what you do. The deepest
and most fundamental layer is identity — what you
believe or who you are. While changes in all three
layers are useful in their own way, the key to lasting
success lies in the direction of change. True
behavior change occurs when there is a shift in your
identity from within. If your new habit is not in
harmony with your identity, it is unlikely to last.
You can work on changing your identity through two
steps. First, keep asking yourself, “What kind of
person do I want to become?” Once you have an
idea of the kind of person you want to be, start
reinforcing that identity through your actions.
Specifically, repeat the action that kind of person
would choose to do, and over time, you will naturally
become such a person. For example, if you want to
start exercising daily, think of yourself as an energetic
and motivated person who cares about his or her
health. Then try to do the routines that such a person
would naturally do. Repeating these routines will
gradually lead you to become that kind of person.

윗글의 내용을 가장 잘 이해한 사람들로 짝지어진 것은?

∎ 지호: Focusing on outcomes or behaviors is
the surest way to make a habit last.
∎ 수아: A single strong action is enough to
complete a shift in your identity.
∎ 민준: To change, you should picture someone you
admire and wait until you feel ready to act.
∎ 해든: Lasting change comes from a shift in
identity that happens from within.
∎ 이도: A habit that does not fit who you
believe you are is unlikely to last.

수아, 해든
지호, 수아

해든, 이도

this link between the cue and the action is
repeated, the more (C)[firmly / loosely] the new
habit will be rooted in your life.

[How to Change]
Make Your Habit an Automatic Loop
After defining your desired identity, you will want
to integrate new habits into your daily routines. It
is worth noting here (A)[what / that] any lasting
habits ⓐ______________________________. To make habits
take effect almost automatically, we need to
understand the concept of the habit loop, which
consists of four steps: cue, craving, response, and
reward. The more smoothly this loop operates, the
more easily the habit is performed. The following
four laws offer practical guidance for each step.
The 1st Law: Cue
“Make an obvious cue for your habit.”
When creating a new habit, set a cue that sparks
the habit and make the cue as (B)[obvious /
obviously] as possible. The two most common cues
are time and location. The formula for your action
plan can be “I will [BEHAVIOR] at [TIME] in
[LOCATION].” Instead of a vague intent like “I will
work out,” (C)[being / be] specific and tell yourself “I
will work out for an hour starting at 8 p.m. at home.”
Another effective method is habit stacking. Your
current habit is already associated with a particular
time and location, so pair it with a new one by
saying something like “After I [CURRENT HABIT], I
will [NEW HABIT].” Your action plan can be “After I
finish dinner around 8 p.m., I’ll immediately change
into my workout clothes.” The more this link
between the cue and the action is repeated, the
more firmly the new habit will be rooted in your life.

body:
[What to Change]
Give Yourself a New Identity
You might find it challenging to develop and maintain good habits for more than a few days. This often happens when people focus on changing external outcomes or behaviors rather than on where they originate from — their inner identity. Behavior change consists of three layers. The outermost layer is outcome — what you achieve. The middle layer is process — what you do. The deepest and most fundamental layer is identity — what you believe or who you are. While changes in all three layers are useful in their own way, the key to lasting success lies in (A)______________________. True behavior change occurs when there is a shift in your identity from within. If your new habit is not in harmony with your identity, it is unlikely to last.

You can work on changing your identity through two steps. First, keep asking yourself, “What kind of person do I want to become?” Once you have an idea of the kind of person you want to be, start reinforcing that identity through your actions. Specifically, repeat the action that kind of person would choose to do, and over time, you will naturally become such a person. For example, if you want to start exercising daily, think of yourself as an energetic and motivated person who cares about his or her health. Then try to do the routines that such a person would naturally do. Repeating these routines will gradually lead you to become that kind of person.

the speed of visible results
the direction of change

Our final destination was Uluru, the largest rock in
the world. I’ve longed to see it ⓐin person ever
since I came across a picture of it a few years ago.
When I finally laid eyes on Uluru after an
exhausting train ride, I couldn’t believe what I was
seeing. Could this ⓑmodest mountain really be a
single piece of rock? From a distance, it looked like
a huge red dome, providing an amazing ⓒcontrast
against the clear blue sky.
 The next day, we walked around its 10-kilometer
base. Along the way, we saw numerous caves, some
of which displayed a distinct gray hue. My uncle
informed me that Uluru was naturally gray, but that
its iron content had ⓓoxidized over time, giving it
its iconic red color.
 The highlight of our visit was the sunset. Prior to
my trip, I had learned that the color of the sunsets
at Uluru changes over time based on the sun’s
position and the intensity of sunlight. When I finally
saw one, the colors transformed from red to deep
orange and then to purple as the sun sank below
the horizon. It was impossible to find words to
describe the beauty I was seeing. It was the most
ⓔmemorable night of my entire journey.

One of the sites I was most excited about was the
Great Barrier Reef, the world’s largest coral reef
system. There are several regions you can visit to
see it, and I chose to explore Lady Elliot Island in
the southern region, which is known for its
beautiful coral reefs and manta rays.
(A) It was a spectacular burst of colors and life! My
uncle later informed me that many parts of the
Great Barrier Reef, especially in the northern
region, suffer from coral bleaching, which turns
the reef white. I felt bad when I heard that and
hoped the reef would recover soon.
(B) As our plane approached land, I spotted the
Great Barrier Reef, stretching as far as I could
see. The water was different shades of blue and
green, depending on the depth of the sea and
the coral formations underneath. Endless patches
of white sand added to the breathtaking
scenery. It was so beautiful, and I couldn’t wait
to dive into the crystal-clear water!
(C) As I wanted to explore the coral reef more
closely, I went snorkeling. The first sight that
greeted me in the water was manta rays. Even
though they are endangered, I witnessed many
mantas gliding elegantly through the water. I
also encountered sea turtles and a school of
tropical fish. It was the coral reef, however, that
impressed me the most that day.

body:
On the first morning of their summer vacation, a young English boy named Jerry and his mother walked together towards their usual beach. But the young boy’s eyes followed the path to a rocky bay that was a bit farther away. Feeling ⓐthat his attention was elsewhere, his mother worried about the ideas that he might be getting. The boy, ⓑnoticed his mother’s concern, smiled at her and continued following along. He kept glancing over his shoulder at the wild bay, however, imagining ⓒwhat it might hold.
The next morning, Jerry’s mother asked him ⓓwhat he was interested in trying another beach. He first answered no, regretting that he ⓔhad made his mother think that he was bored with their usual place. As they were walking, however, he suddenly changed his mind and said, “I’d like to go and have a look at those rocks down there.” She gave the idea some thought. The area he was pointing to looked somewhat dangerous, but she decided it would be fine ⓕto let him go on his own. As his mother walked away, Jerry felt like running after her again and ⓖenjoyed the beach as they had always done, but he did not.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓑ noticed → noticing (완전한 절(The boy ~ along)을 이루는 주어 The boy와 동사 smiled 사이에 이중 콤마로 삽입된 분사구문으로, 의미상 주어인 The boy가 어머니의 걱정을 ‘알아차린‘ 주체이므로 noticed를 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 noticing으로 고친다.)
ⓓ what → if 또는 whether (뒤에 완전한 절(he ~ beach)을 이끌어 ask의 직접목적어인 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 what은 쓸 수 없으며, 흐름상 ’~인지 아닌지 그에게 물었다‘의 의미가 되어야 자연스러우므로, ’~인지 아닌지‘의 의미를 갖는 명사절 접속사 if 또는 whether로 고친다.)
ⓖ enjoyed → enjoying (흐름상 ’뒤따라가서 해변을 즐기고 싶었다‘라는 뜻으로 felt like의 목적어 running과 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되어야 하므로 enjoyed를 enjoying으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 완전한 절(his attention was elsewhere)을 이끌어 분사 Feeling의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that은 적절하다.
ⓒ 분사 imagining의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로, ’의문사+주어+동사 ~‘의 어순을 갖는 간접의문문을 이끄는 의문사 what이 쓰인 것은 적절하며, what은 의문사이자 hold의 목적어 역할을 함께 하고 있다.
ⓔ 평소 가던 곳에 싫증이 났다고 어머니가 생각하게 만든 것이 후회를 하는 과거 시점보다 먼저 발생한 것이므로 과거 시제보다 앞설 때 사용하는 과거완료 had made는 적절하다.
ⓕ decided의 목적어 역할을 하는, 접속사 that이 생략된 명사절의 주어 자리 it은 가주어이므로, 이에 상응하는 진주어로 to부정사 to let이 쓰인 것은 적절하다.

body:
Reaching the rocky bay, he started swimming but soon felt somewhat lonely being so far from his mother. After some time, he encountered a group of local boys who were diving from the rocks. They were around his age, and he desperately wanted to become friends with them. He swam closer, and they turned to watch him. One smiled and waved him over. They showed him how to dive from the rocks into the deep water. He tried ⓐdiving with them, but he was too afraid.
(A) At fifty, he started to worry. At one hundred, he wondered whether he should yell for help. But around one hundred and fifty, he realized that they were in fact swimming through some rocks in the water and coming out the other side.
(B) Feeling ⓑrejected, Jerry watched the boys from a distance and noticed that they were underwater for a long time. He started counting the seconds.
(C) ⓒNoticed his hesitation, the boys soon lost interest. Jerry tried calling out to them in the local language, “Bonjour! Merci! Monsieur, monsieur!” but they ignored him and swam away.
After they left, he tried to do what they ⓓhad done, but when he tried to open his eyes to see underwater, his eyes stung from the salty water. With his eyes closed, however, he was unable to see the tunnel that the boys had swum through. His only option was to give up and ⓔgo home.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: Jerry가 소년들과 함께 다이빙을 시도했으나 너무 두려워했다는 주어진 글 뒤에, 두려워서 하지 못한 다이빙을 his hesitation(그의 망설임)으로 이어받아 소년들이 흥미를 잃고 Jerry의 외침을 무시한 채 헤엄쳐 떠나는 상황을 설명하는 (C), 이 상황을 Feeling rejected(거절당했다고 느끼며)로 이어받아 소년들이 물속에 오랫동안 있는 것을 보고 초를 세기 시작했다는 내용의 (B), 초를 세는 행동을 50초, 100초, 150초 등의 구체적인 수치와 함께 설명하며 소년들이 물속의 바위 사이로 헤엄쳐 반대편으로 나오고 있음을 깨닫는 (A)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

solution:
ⓒNoticed → Noticing (완전한 절(the boys ~ Merci!)과 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 the boys가 그의 망설임을 ‘알아차린’ 주체이므로 Noticed를 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 Noticing으로 고친다.)

body:
Back home that evening, Jerry asked his mother for swimming goggles. After receiving them the next day, he ran off back to the bay. Underwater, he was now able to see the tunnel clearly. He tried to enter it, but the darkness and the feeling of seaweed on his skin frightened him. He gave up and decided to ______.
From that day forward, every morning, the boy left his mother at the beach and came to the rocks to practice his breathing and diving. Some days, he pushed himself too hard, and his nose would bleed from too much practice. His mother told him that she was worried about him and had him join her at their usual beach. But the beach looked different to him now. It now seemed like a place for small children.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: ask the local boys to guide him
find another route to get inside the tunnel
practice holding his breath underwater instead
focus on making some lasting memories with his mother
wait until he was older and stronger before trying again
solution:
Jerry는 물속에서 굴을 보았지만 어둠과 피부에 닿는 해초의 느낌 때문에 두려움을 느껴 포기했으나 이후 매일 아침 어머니와 떨어져 바위로 가서 호흡과 다이빙을 연습했다고 했으므로, 빈칸에는 굴에 다시 도전하기 위해 수중 호흡 능력을 향상하는 데 집중했다는 내용이 와야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ③ ‘대신 물속에서 숨 참는 연습을 하다’가 적절하다.
오답
① 현지 소년들에게 자신을 안내해줄 것을 요청하다
② 굴 안으로 들어가기 위해 다른 경로를 찾다
④ 어머니와 오래 남을 추억을 만드는 데 집중하다
⑤ 다시 시도하기 전에 나이가 더 들고 힘이 더 세질 때까지 기다리다

body:
[1]
Jerry soon began to feel restless being back at the beach with his mother, and he worried that all the practice he had put in would go to waste. The next day, he decided to go back to the rocky bay. He now spent his days exploring the tunnel at the bay and practicing his breathing whenever he was back with his mother. (A)그는 준비가 되어 있는 것이 자신을 좌절하게 했던 굴을 자신이 정복하는 데 도움이 되리라는 것을 알았다.
[2]
After a few days, his mother told him that they would soon need to return home. This news urged him to go back to the bay. He felt that he absolutely needed to go through the tunnel before they went home. His fear, however, made him think that just practicing some more and trying again next year might be wiser.
But even after reaching that conclusion, he found himself sitting on the rock with a longing to overcome his fear and conquer the tunnel. It would be now or never. He decided to try once more. His hands were shaking, but he placed them firmly at his sides. He looked up at the sky, filled his lungs with air, and then sank fast into the ocean.

윗글의 내용과 (A)~(E)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?
(A) The day after staying at the beach with his mother, Jerry returned to the rocky bay because he did not want his practice to be wasted. (T/F)
(B) Whenever he was with his mother, Jerry explored the underwater tunnel and practiced holding his breath. (T/F)
(C) When his mother announced that they would soon return home, Jerry felt he had to pass through the tunnel before they left. (T/F)
(D) Although Jerry wanted to conquer the tunnel, he decided to postpone his next attempt until the following year. (T/F)
(E) Despite his trembling hands, Jerry took a deep breath and quickly sank into the ocean. (T/F)
choices: T-F-T-F-F
T-F-T-F-T
F-T-T-F-T
T-F-F-T-T
F-F-F-T-T
solution:
차례대로 T-F-T-F-T이다.
(A) 어머니와 함께 해변에서 머문 다음 날, Jerry는 자신의 연습이 헛수고가 되는 것을 원하지 않았기 때문에 바위투성이의 만으로 돌아갔다. (일치)
(B) Jerry는 어머니와 함께 있을 때마다 수중 굴을 탐험하고 숨을 참는 연습을 했다(→만에서는 굴을 탐험하고, 어머니와 다시 함께 있을 때마다 호흡 연습을 했다). (불일치)
(C) 어머니가 곧 집으로 돌아갈 것이라고 알렸을 때, Jerry는 그들이 떠나기 전에 반드시 굴을 통과해야 한다고 느꼈다. (일치)
(D) Jerry는 굴을 정복하고 싶었지만, 다음 시도를 내년까지 미루기로 결정했다(→미루는 것이 현명할지도 모른다고 생각했지만, 지금이 아니면 절대 할 수 없을 것 같아서 다시 시도했다). (불일치)
(E) 떨리는 손에도 불구하고, Jerry는 깊이 숨을 마시고 바닷속으로 빠르게 가라앉았다. (일치)

His mother’s eyes lit up, as she was happy to see him back. “Did you have a nice morning?” she asked. Jerry replied with ⓓpride, “Mom, I can stay underwater for two minutes, three minutes, at least!” His mom thought about telling him to rest for the remainder of the day, but she didn’t have to. He was now ⓔreluctant to stay home and rest. (C)[Go / Going] to the bay was no longer important to him.

solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘어머니는 Jerry의 관심이 다른 곳에 있다고 느끼고, 그가 무슨 생각을 하고 있을지 걱정했다.’라는 뜻으로, 그의 관심이 다른 곳에 있었다고 했으므로 이 문장 앞에는 Jerry가 시선 또는 관심을 다른 곳으로 돌리는 행동이 제시되어야 한다. M: Black holes are the strangest objects in the universe. They are regions in space with strong gravity that (A)[is / are] so powerful that even light cannot escape it. Black holes are formed when stars collapse. One interesting fact about them is (B)[what / that] black holes are invisible. So how do we know that they exist? We can detect black holes by their gravitational influence. For example, if a star comes close to a black hole, its enormous gravity will begin to pull in the star instantly. When black holes swallow up stars, powerful energy is created. The light from this energy can (C)[detect / be detected] from great distances with telescopes. The first photograph of a black hole was taken by the Event Horizon Telescope in 2019. This was a major breakthrough and has had a huge impact on the scientific community.
위 담화의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

are / that / be detected
is / what / be detected
is / that / detect

solution:
(A) 주격 관계대명사 that 뒤에 이어진 관계사절의 동사 자리이며, 선행사가 단수명사구 detect이므로 be동사 단수형인 is는 적절하다.
(B) 완전한 절(black holes are invisible)을 이끌어 be동사 is 뒤의 주격 보어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 명사절 접속사 that이 적절하다.
(C) 주어 The light가 ‘감지되는’ 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없이 전치사구(from ~ telescopes)가 이어지고 있으므로 조동사 can 뒤에서 수동태(be+p.p.)를 이루는 be detected가 적절하다.

body:
Since ancient times, we have looked to the sky with wonder, curious about what lies beyond our world. This inherent desire ⓐto explore the universe has encouraged technological innovations that can aid us in this pursuit. Among these advancements ⓑare space telescopes and space robots, which have paved the way for our journey toward understanding the mysteries of space.
When we observe space from the ground, Earth’s atmosphere creates obstacles for our vision. It absorbs specific types of lights such as ultraviolet and infrared, causing distortions in our observations and making some objects beyond the atmosphere ⓒinvisible. Consequently, the space ⓓwhere we see from Earth’s surface can differ significantly from its actual appearance. To overcome these limitations, telescopes are launched into space beyond Earth’s atmosphere.
Space telescopes are specifically designed to capture a spectrum of light that is not visible on Earth. This capability provides us with a clear and uninterrupted view of celestial objects, allowing us to better observe stars, black holes, and galaxies ⓔlocated billions of light years away from Earth. The data and images gathered by space telescopes are invaluable to scientists, enabling them ⓕstudying the birth and death of celestial bodies and their unique characteristics.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 2개
3개
4개
5개
6개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓓ where → that 또는 which (동사 see의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(we ~ surface)을 이끌어 선행사 the space를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 where는 목적격 관계대명사 that 또는 which로 고친다.)
*ⓓ는 원래 지문에서 생략되어 있음
ⓕ studying → to study (현재분사 enabling, 목적어 them에 이어져 ‘enable+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리이므로, studying을 to부정사 to study로 고친다.)

Since ancient times, we have looked to the sky with wonder, curious about what lies beyond our world. This inherent desire ⓐto explore the universe has encouraged technological innovations that can aid us in this pursuit. Among these advancements ⓑare space telescopes and space robots, which have paved the way for our journey toward understanding the mysteries of space.
When we observe space from the ground, Earth’s atmosphere creates obstacles for our vision. It absorbs specific types of lights such as ultraviolet and infrared, causing distortions in our observations and making some objects beyond the atmosphere ⓒinvisible. Consequently, the space ⓓwhere we see from Earth’s surface can differ significantly from its actual appearance. To overcome these limitations, telescopes are launched into space beyond Earth’s atmosphere.
Space telescopes are specifically designed to capture a spectrum of light that is not visible on Earth. This capability provides us with a clear and uninterrupted view of celestial objects, allowing us to better observe stars, black holes, and galaxies ⓔlocated billions of light years away from Earth. The data and images gathered by space telescopes are invaluable to scientists, enabling them ⓕstudying the birth and death of celestial bodies and their unique characteristics.

Space telescopes and space robots help us understand the mysteries of space.
Earth's atmosphere makes it difficult for us to see space clearly from the ground.

Among the various space telescopes in operation, the Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990, stands out as an unprecedented achievement in space technology. ⓐOrbiting approximately 600 kilometers above Earth’s atmosphere, Hubble has transmitted incredibly detailed images of space, revolutionizing our understanding of the universe. It has played a crucial role in (A)facilitating pioneering discoveries about the relationships between celestial bodies, the formation of galaxies, and the expansion of the universe. Moreover, its breathtaking images have sparked people’s imaginations and ⓑmade space exploration an even more intriguing journey.
To prepare for Hubble’s retirement, the James Webb Space Telescope was launched as its (B)predecessor in 2021. Webb is a state-of-the-art space telescope with capabilities superior to ⓒthat of any other telescope. It features a honeycomb-patterned mirror that is about three times larger in diameter than Hubble’s round-shaped mirror, resulting in an image collection area that is 6.25 times (C)wider. Positioned 1.5 million kilometers from Earth, Webb orbits the Sun alongside Earth, while Hubble orbits Earth itself. Webb also specializes in capturing infrared light, ⓓwhich can pass through dusty regions more (D)effectively than the visible light used by Hubble. These features enable Webb to offer a view of space with greatly (E)enhanced clarity and minimal interference. As Webb continues its mission, it is expected ⓔto offer deeper insights into the birth of the universe and the evolutionary processes following the Big Bang.

ⓓ 콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(can ~ Hubble)을 이끌어 앞의 명사구 infrared light를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which는 적절하다.

body:
Another widely recognized type of space robot is the rover, a robotic vehicle designed to move across the surface of planets and moons to explore their environments. ⓐ다양한 과학 장비를 갖춘 로버는 마치 움직이는 실험실과 같은 기능을 하면서 이동 중에 실험과 조사를 수행한다. An iconic example is Curiosity, which landed on Mars in 2012. This car-sized rover made significant discoveries about Mars’s past. It found signs of a water stream on a crater’s floor and identified chemicals such as carbon in a powder sample drilled from a rock. These findings suggest the possibility that some form of life might (A)[have existed / exist] on Mars in the past.
While humanoid robots, (B)[which / what] resemble humans in structure and movement, have not yet become common in space exploration, there have been significant advancements in this area as well. A humanoid robot (C)[naming / named] Robonaut 2 was sent to work on the International Space Station in 2011. Robonaut 2 was designed to assist astronauts in spacewalks and perform various tasks in dangerous environments. Despite their diversity, these robots share a common mission: to fearlessly venture into the unexplored territories of the universe.
As we journey through the vast universe, telescopes and robots have been our eyes and hands. Their lenses and sensors reveal the beauty and mysteries of galaxies, planets, and celestial wonders. As technology advances, we find ourselves closer to the secrets of the universe than ever before. The future of space exploration promises wonders beyond our imagination, and this fills us with great excitement.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: have existed / which / naming
exist / what / naming
have existed / which / named
exist / which / named
have existed / what / named
solution:
(A) 과거 시점을 나타내는 부사구 in the past가 있으므로 앞의 조동사 might와 함께 과거에 일어난 일에 대한 약한 추측을 나타내는 ‘조동사+have+p.p.’를 이루는 have existed가 적절하다.
(B) 콤마(,) 뒤에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(resemble ~ movement)을 이끌어 앞의 명사구 humanoid robots를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 계속적 용법의 주격 관계대명사 which가 적절하다.
(C) 주어 A humanoid robot을 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사 자리로, 수식을 받는 A humanoid robot은 ‘이름 지어진’ 대상이며 뒤에 ’name A B(A를 B라고 이름 짓다)‘의 5형식 구조에서 name의 목적어 없이 목적격보어에 해당하는 Robonaut 2가 이어지므로 수동 표현인 ’A be named B(A가 B라고 이름 지어지다)‘를 이루는 과거분사 named 적절하다.

(A) Unlike robots, human astronauts must undergo rigorous and lengthy training programs to prepare for the physical challenges of spaceflight. (B) A variety of robots have been developed for space missions. (C) Some are designed to land on celestial bodies, while others are built for flyby missions. (D) Some robots remain in fixed positions, while others are engineered for mobility. (E) Robots also come in a range of shapes, resembling those of spacecraft, vehicles, or even humans. They are categorized and named according to their specific functions.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 관계없는 문장은?
solution: 우주 탐사에서 인간 우주비행사보다 로봇을 활용하는 것이 더 안전하고 비용 효율적이라는 점을 설명한 뒤, 우주 탐사에 사용되는 로봇의 임무 방식, 이동성, 형태 등 다양한 특징을 소개하는 글이다. (B)에서 우주 임무를 위해 다양한 종류의 로봇이 개발되었으며, (C)에서 로봇마다 천체 착륙이나 천체 근접 비행 등 수행하는 임무 방식이 다르며, (D)에서 로봇마다 고정된 위치에 머무르거나 이동할 수 있도록 설계되는 등 이동성에 차이가 있으며, (E)에서 로봇은 우주선, 차량, 인간 등을 닮은 다양한 형태를 가지며 구체적인 기능에 따라 분류되고 명명된다는 점을 설명하고 있다. 그러나 (A) ‘로봇과는 달리, 인간 우주비행사들은 우주 비행의 신체적 어려움에 대비하기 위해 엄격하고 장기간의 훈련 프로그램을 받아야 한다.’는 인간 우주비행사의 훈련 과정에 초점을 맞추고 있으므로 로봇을 활용하는 이유와 로봇의 특징과 기능을 설명하는 내용 사이에서 흐름을 방해하므로 (A)는 전체 글의 흐름과 관계없다.

body:
When we observe space from the ground, Earth’s atmosphere creates obstacles for our vision. It absorbs specific types of lights such as ultraviolet and infrared, causing distortions in our observations and making some objects beyond the atmosphere invisible. (A)______, the space we see from Earth’s surface can differ significantly from its actual appearance. To overcome these limitations, telescopes are launched into space beyond Earth’s atmosphere.
Space telescopes are specifically designed to capture a spectrum of light that is not visible on Earth. This capability provides us with a clear and uninterrupted view of celestial objects, allowing us to better observe stars, black holes, and galaxies located billions of light years away from Earth. The data and images gathered by space telescopes are invaluable to scientists, enabling them to study the birth and death of celestial bodies and their unique characteristics.
Among the various space telescopes in operation, the Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990, stands out as an unprecedented achievement in space technology. Orbiting approximately 600 kilometers above Earth’s atmosphere, Hubble has transmitted incredibly detailed images of space, revolutionizing our understanding of the universe. It has played a crucial role in facilitating pioneering discoveries about the relationships between celestial bodies, the formation of galaxies, and the expansion of the universe. (B)______, its breathtaking images have sparked people’s imaginations and made space exploration an even more intriguing journey.
윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
choices: Nevertheless / Furthermore
As a result / That is
For example / In other words
Consequently / Moreover
For instance / Therefore
solution:
(A) 지구 대기는 자외선과 적외선과 같은 특정 유형의 빛을 흡수하여 관측을 왜곡하고 대기권 너머의 일부 천체를 보이지 않게 만든다는 내용 뒤에서 그 결과에 해당하는 내용인 이러한 대기의 영향으로 지구 표면에서 관찰하는 우주의 모습이 실제 모습과 상당히 달라질 수 있다는 내용이 제시되므로, 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 인과간계를 연결하는 As a result(그 결과) 또는 Consequently(결과적으로)가 적절하다.
(B) Hubble 우주 망원경이 우주에 대한 인류의 이해를 넓히고 천체의 관계, 은하의 형성, 우주의 팽창에 관한 중요한 발견을 가능하게 했다는 점을 설명한 뒤, Hubble 망원경의 아름다운 이미지가 사람들의 상상력을 자극하고 우주 탐사를 더욱 흥미로운 여정으로 만들었다는 Hubble 망원경의 또 다른 긍정적인 기여를 덧붙이고 있으므로, 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 추가적인 정보를 덧붙이는 연결어 Furthermore(게다가) 또는 Moreover(게다가)가 적절하다.
오답
① 그럼에도 불구하고 게다가
② 그 결과 다시 말해서
③ 예를 들어 다시 말해서
⑤ 예를 들어 그러므로

body:
These features enable Webb to offer a view of space with greatly enhanced clarity and minimal interference.
To prepare for Hubble’s retirement, the James Webb Space Telescope was launched as its successor in 2021. (A) Webb is a state-of-the-art space telescope with capabilities superior to those of any other telescope. (B) It features a honeycomb-patterned mirror that is about three times larger in diameter than Hubble’s round-shaped mirror, resulting in an image collection area that is 6.25 times wider. (C) Positioned 1.5 million kilometers from Earth, Webb orbits the Sun alongside Earth, while Hubble orbits Earth itself. (D) Webb also specializes in capturing infrared light, which can pass through dusty regions more effectively than the visible light used by Hubble. (E) As Webb continues its mission, it is expected to offer deeper insights into the birth of the universe and the evolutionary processes following the Big Bang.
다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘이러한 특징들은 Webb이 크게 향상된 선명도와 최소한의 간섭으로 우주의 경관을 제공할 수 있게 한다.’라는 뜻으로, These features(이러한 특징들)가 쓰였으므로, 이 문장 앞에는 Webb이 더 선명하고 방해가 적은 우주 관측을 가능하게 하는 특징들이 언급되어야 한다. (C) 앞에서 언급된 Hubble보다 약 3배 큰 지름의 거울과 6.25배 넓은 이미지 수집 면적, (D) 앞에서 언급된 지구에서 150만 킬로미터 떨어진 곳에서 지구와 함께 태양을 공전하는 위치적 특징, (E) 앞에서 언급된 먼지가 많은 구역을 더 효과적으로 통과할 수 있는 적외선 포착 능력은 모두 우주를 더 선명하게, 관측을 방해하는 요소를 최소화하면서 볼 수 있게 하는 특징들이므로, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은 이 세 가지 특징이 모두 제시된 뒤이자, 이러한 능력으로 인해 기대되는 결과를 설명하는 내용 앞인 (E)이다.

body:
Thorough space exploration goes beyond (A)[direct / remote] observations and includes up-close examinations of celestial bodies, material collection, and on-site experiments. While human astronauts can be sent on these missions, it is often safer and more cost-effective to use robots. Robots can better withstand the harsh conditions of space, including extreme temperatures and high radiation levels that can pose serious risks to human astronauts.
A variety of robots have been developed for space missions. Some are designed to land on celestial bodies, while others are built for flyby missions. Some robots remain in (B)[movable / fixed] positions, while others are engineered for mobility. Robots also come in a range of shapes, resembling those of spacecraft, vehicles, or even humans. They are categorized and named according to their specific functions.
Probes are one notable type of space robots. These spacecraft-like robots are designed to capture photos and gather data without needing to land on celestial bodies. For example, the twin Voyagers launched in 1977 are historic probes. These probes successfully flew by the major outer planets of our solar system — Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune — discovering numerous fascinating details about them. One of the Voyagers’ significant findings was the presence of highly active volcanoes on Io, one of Jupiter’s moons, marking the first evidence of geological processes observed on other planets. After completing their planetary missions, these probes (C)[ended / continued] their journey beyond our solar system. Voyager 1 first entered interstellar space in 2012 and became the farthest human-made object from Earth.
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: remote / fixed / ended
direct / movable / ended
remote / fixed / continued
remote / movable / continued
direct / fixed / continued
solution:
(A) 우주 탐사는 천체에 직접 접근하여 자세히 조사하고, 물질을 수집하며, 현장에서 실험을 수행하는 활동까지 포함한다는 내용이 이어지고 있으므로 직접 접근하여 수행하는 탐사와 대비되는 관찰 방식을 나타내는 remote(원격의)가 적절하다.
direct 직접적인
(B) 다른 로봇들은 이동할 수 있도록 설계되었다는 내용과 역접을 나타내는 while(반면에)로 연결되어 있으므로, 이동하는 것과 대비되는 fixed(고정된)가 적절하다.
movable 움직일 수 있는
(C) 성간 우주에 진입하여 지구에서 가장 멀리 떨어진 인간이 만든 물체가 되었다는 내용이 이어지고 있으므로 여정을 계속 했다는 흐름을 이루는 continued(계속 했다)가 적절하다.
ended 끝냈다

that / inspiring / where
what / inspired / which
that / inspired / where
that / inspiring / which
solution:
(A) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(have ~ lessons)을 이끌어 명사 books를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 주격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다.
(B) 명사구 discussion session을 수식하는 분사 자리이며, discussion session이 ‘영감을 주는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 inspiring이 적절하다.
(C) 콤마(,) 뒤에서 완전한 절(you ~ potential)을 이끌어 선행사 creative writing classes를 부연 설명하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 관계부사 where가 적절하다.

On the first morning of their summer vacation, a young English boy ⓐnamed Jerry and his mother walked together towards their usual beach. But the young boy’s eyes followed the path to a rocky bay that was a bit farther away. Feeling that his attention was elsewhere, his mother worried about the ideas that he might be getting. The boy, noticing his mother’s concern, ⓑsmiling at her and continued following along. He kept glancing over his shoulder at the wild bay, however, ⓒimagining what it might hold.
The next morning, Jerry’s mother asked him if he was interested in trying another beach. He first answered no, regretting that he had made his mother ⓓthink that he was bored with their usual place. As they were walking, however, he suddenly changed his mind and said, “I’d like to go and have a look at those rocks down there.” She gave the idea some thought. The area he was pointing to looked somewhat dangerous, but she decided it would be fine to let him go on his own. As his mother walked away, Jerry felt like running after her again and enjoying the beach as they ⓔhave always done, but he did not.

Jerry’s mother was ______ that he might be ______ in the rocky bay, which seemed ______, and he continued to pay ______ to it and eventually decided to explore the area instead of enjoying the ______ beach.

body:
On the first morning of their summer vacation, a young English boy named Jerry and his mother walked together towards their usual beach. But the young boy’s eyes followed the path to a rocky bay that was a bit farther away. Feeling that his attention was elsewhere, his mother worried about the ideas that he might be getting.
(A) The next morning, Jerry’s mother asked him if he was interested in trying another beach. He first answered no, ⓐregretted that he had made his mother think that he was bored with their usual place.
(B) The boy, noticing his mother’s concern, smiled at her and continued following along. He kept glancing over his shoulder at the wild bay, however, imagining what it might hold.
(C) As they were walking, however, he suddenly changed his mind and said, “I’d like to go and have a look at those rocks down there.” She gave the idea some thought.
The area he was pointing to looked somewhat dangerous, but she decided it would be fine to let him ⓑgo on his own. As his mother walked away, Jerry felt like running after her again and ⓒenjoying the beach as they had always done, but he did not.
Reaching the rocky bay, he started swimming but soon felt somewhat lonely being so far from his mother. After some time, he encountered a group of local boys ⓓwho were diving from the rocks. They were around his age, and he desperately wanted to become friends with them. He swam closer, and they turned ⓔto watch him. One smiled and waved him over. They showed him how to dive from the rocks into the deep water. He tried diving with them, but he was too afraid. Noticing his hesitation, the boys soon lost interest. Jerry tried calling out to them in the local language, “Bonjour! Merci! Monsieur, monsieur!” but they ignored him and swam away.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 어머니는 Jerry의 관심이 다른 곳에 있음을 느끼고, 그가 어떤 생각을 하고 있을지 걱정했다는 주어진 글 뒤에, 어머니의 걱정을 his mother’s concern(그의 어머니의 걱정)으로 이어받아 Jerry가 이를 알아차리고 미소를 지으며 계속 따라가면서도 바위투성이의 만을 흘끗 바라보는 모습을 묘사하는 (B), Jerry가 다른 곳에 관심을 보인 것과 관련하여 다음 날 아침 어머니가 다른 해변에 가 보고 싶은지 묻자, Jerry는 어머니가 평소 가던 해변에 싫증을 느낀다고 생각하게 만든 것을 후회하며 아니라고 답하는 (A), however(그러나)를 통해 Jerry가 갑자기 마음을 바꾸어 바위가 있는 곳에 가 보고 싶다고 말하는 (C)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓐ regretted → regretting (완전한 절(He first answered no)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 연결되므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 He가 ‘후회하는‘ 주체이므로 regretted를 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 regretting으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓑ to let의 목적격보어 자리이며, 사역동사 let은 ’let+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형)‘의 구문으로 쓰이므로 목적격보어 자리의 동사원형 go는 적절하다.
ⓒ ’다시 그녀를 뒤따라가서 해변을 즐기고 싶었다’의 의미로, ‘~하고 싶다’를 뜻하는 ‘feel like+-ing’ 구문의 running과 등위접속사 and로 병렬로 연결되므로, enjoying은 적절하다.
ⓓ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(were ~ rocks)을 이끌어 사람을 나타내는 선행사 local boys를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로 주격 관계대명사 who는 적절하다.
ⓔ 완전한 절(they turned)에 접속사 없이 이어지므로 준동사 자리이며, 흐름상 ‘그를 보기 위해’라는 목적의 의미를 나타내므로 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to watch는 적절하다.

body:
Back home that evening, Jerry asked his mother for swimming goggles. After receiving them the next day, he ran off back to the bay. Underwater, he was now able to see the tunnel clearly. He tried to enter it, but the darkness and the feeling of seaweed on his skin frightened him. He gave up and decided to practice holding his breath underwater instead.
From that day forward, every morning, the boy left his mother at the beach and came to the rocks to practice his breathing and diving. Some days, he pushed himself too hard, and his nose would bleed from too much practice. His mother told him that she was worried about him and had him join her at their usual beach. But the beach looked different to him now. It now seemed like a place for small children.
Jerry soon began to feel restless being back at the beach with his mother, and he worried that ______. The next day, he decided to go back to the rocky bay. He now spent his days exploring the tunnel at the bay and practicing his breathing whenever he was back with his mother. He knew that being prepared would help him conquer the tunnel that had defeated him.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: his mother would forbid him from swimming
the local boys would forget about him entirely
he might injure himself without proper equipment
his dedicated effort would end up being meaningless
he would miss the opportunity to spend more time with his mother
solution:
Jerry는 굴에 들어가는 데 실패한 뒤 매일 아침 바위투성이의 만에서 숨 참기와 다이빙을 연습했으며, 때로는 코피가 날 정도로 무리하기도 했다. 그러나 어머니와 평소 가던 해변에 머물게 되자 안절부절못하기 시작했고, 결국 다시 바위투성이의 만으로 돌아가 굴 탐험과 숨 참기 연습을 다시 이어서 했으며, 그는 준비가 되어 있어야 자신을 좌절하게 했던 굴을 정복하는 데 도움이 되리라는 것을 알고 있다고 했으므로, 빈칸에는 그동안 자신이 쏟아부은 연습과 노력이 무용지물이 될까 봐 걱정했다는 흐름이 들어가는 것이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ④ ‘그의 헌신적인 노력이 결국 아무 의미가 없게 될 것이다’가 적절하다.
본문변형 all the practice he had put in would go to waste → his dedicated effort would end up being meaningless
오답
① 어머니가 그가 수영하는 것을 금지할 것이다
② 현지 소년들이 그를 완전히 잊을 것이다
③ 적절한 장비 없이는 그가 다칠 수도 있다
⑤ 어머니와 더 많은 시간을 보낼 기회를 놓칠 것이다

After a few days, his mother told him (A)[what / that] they would soon need to return home. This news urged him (B)[going / to go] back to the bay. He felt that he absolutely needed to go through the tunnel before they went home. ⓐ하지만 그의 두려움은 그저 연습을 좀 더 하고 내년에 다시 시도하는 것이 더 현명할지도 모른다고 생각하게 만들었다.
But even after reaching that conclusion, he found himself (C)[sit / sitting] on the rock with a longing to overcome his fear and conquer the tunnel. It would be now or never. 윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: that / to go / sitting
what / going / sitting
that / to go / sit
what / to go / sit
that / going / sitting
solution:
(A) 완전한 절(they ~ home)을 이끌어 동사 told의 직접목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that이 적절하다.
(B) urged의 목적격보어 자리이며, 동사 urged는 ‘urge+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이므로 to부정사 to go가 적절하다.

다음 글의 내용과 (A)~(E)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?
(A) Being far from his mother made Jerry feel a little lonely shortly after he began swimming at the rocky bay. (T/F)
(B) While diving into the deep water from the rocks, Jerry came across a group of local boys around his age. (T/F)
(C) As Jerry swam closer, the boys ignored him and swam away before he could even reach them. (T/F)
(D) The boys lost interest in Jerry when they realized that he was too frightened to dive with them. (T/F)
(E) Jerry attempted to get their attention by shouting a few words in their language, but they paid no attention and swam away. (T/F)
choices: T-F-T-T-F
F-T-T-F-T
T-F-F-T-F
T-F-F-F-T
T-F-F-T-T
solution:
차례대로 T-F-F-T-T이다.
(A) Jerry가 바위투성이 만에서 수영을 시작한 직후, 어머니에게서 멀리 떨어져 있다는 것은 조금 외롭게 느껴졌다. (일치)
(B) 바위에서 깊은 물속으로 다이빙하는 동안(→바위투성이 만에서 수영하는 동안), Jerry는 자신과 나이가 비슷한 한 무리의 현지 소년들을 우연히 만났다. (불일치)
(C) Jerry가 더 가까이 헤엄쳐 갔을 때, 소년들은 그를 무시하고 그가 그들에게 도착하기도 전에 헤엄쳐 가 버렸다(→그들은 그를 보려고 돌아섰고 한 명이 미소 지으며 그에게 손을 흔들었다). (불일치)
(D) 소년들은 Jerry가 너무 두려워 그들과 함께 다이빙을 할 수 없다는 것을 알아차렸을 때 Jerry에게 관심을 잃었다. (일치)
(E) Jerry는 그들의 언어로 몇 마디 외쳐 그들의 관심을 끌려고 했지만, 그들은 아무런 주의를 기울이지 않고 헤엄쳐 가 버렸다. (일치)

solution:

ⓓ 전치사 After에 이어지는 목적어 자리이며 뒤에 대명사 them이 있으므로 목적어를 취할 수 있는 동명사 receiving은 적절하다.

body:
Jerry soon began to feel restless being back at the beach with his mother, and he worried that all the practice he had put in would go to waste. The next day, he decided to go back to the rocky bay. He now spent his days exploring the tunnel at the bay and practicing his breathing whenever he was back with his mother. He knew that being prepared would help him conquer the tunnel that had defeated him.
After a few days, his mother told him that they would soon need to return home. This news urged him to go back to the bay. He felt that he absolutely needed to go through the tunnel before they went home. His fear, however, made him think that just practicing some more and trying again next year might be wiser.
But even after reaching that conclusion, he found himself sitting on the rock with a longing to overcome his fear and conquer the tunnel. It would be now or never. He decided to try once more. His hands were shaking, but he placed them firmly at his sides. He looked up at the sky, filled his lungs with air, and then sank fast into the ocean.

body:
He soon found the entrance to the tunnel. He took the edges of the hole in his hands and drew himself into it. It was pitch black, but he kept counting, just as he had practiced. Fifty, fifty-one, fifty-two… Soon he reached a hundred, a hundred and one… He kept moving through the tunnel, and when he thought he couldn’t last any longer, he spotted a crack of light at the end. The feeling of victory filled him as he realized that with a few more strokes, he would be coming out the other side. He felt like he was running out of air, but he kept kicking and thinking just a little bit more!
Finally, his hands found the exit of the tunnel, and he swam out into the open sea. At first, he started to gasp like a fish out of water, but after some time, his heart quieted and his eyes cleared. He had made it. After resting a short while on the warm rock, he got on his feet and walked back home. His mother’s eyes lit up, as she was happy to see him back. “Did you have a nice morning?” she asked. Jerry replied with pride, “Mom, I can stay underwater for two minutes, three minutes, at least!” His mom thought about telling him to rest for the remainder of the day, but she didn’t have to. He was now happy to stay home and rest. Going to the bay was no longer important to him.

When we observe space from the ground, Earth’s atmosphere creates obstacles for our vision. It absorbs specific types of lights such as ultraviolet and infrared, (A)[causes / causing] distortions in our observations and making some objects beyond the atmosphere invisible. Consequently, the space we see from Earth’s surface can differ significantly from its actual appearance. To overcome these limitations, telescopes are launched into space beyond Earth’s atmosphere.
Space telescopes are specifically designed to capture a spectrum of light (B)[what / that] is not visible on Earth. This capability provides us with a clear and uninterrupted view of celestial objects, allowing us to better (C)[observe / observing] stars, black holes, and galaxies located billions of light years away from Earth. The data and images gathered by space telescopes are invaluable to scientists, enabling them to study the birth and death of celestial bodies and their unique characteristics.

choices: causes that observe

causes what observe

solution:
(A) 동사가 있는 완전한 절(It ~ infrared)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 이어지고 있으며 등위접속사 and로 분사구문(making ~ invisible)과 병렬 구조를 이루고 있으므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이고, 주절의 주어와 동일한 의미상 주어인 Earth’s atmosphere이 ‘일으키는’ 주체이며 목적어인 명사 distortions가 이어지고 있으므로 능동의 의미인 현재분사 causing이 적절하다.
(B) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(is not visible on Earth)을 이끌어 명사구 a spectrum of light를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 주격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다.
(C) 현재분사 allowing과 목적어 us에 이어져 ’allow+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)(~가 …할 수 있게 하다)‘의 5형식 구문을 이루는 목적격보어 자리이므로, 부사 better 앞의 to와 함께 쓰여 to부정사를 이루는 동사원형 observe가 적절하다. 참고로 동사원형을 수식하는 부사가 to와 동사원형 사이에 온 분리부정사의 형태이다.

body:
Among the various space telescopes in operation, the Hubble Space Telescope, ⓐlaunched in 1990, stands out as an unprecedented achievement in space technology. Orbiting approximately 600 kilometers above Earth’s atmosphere, Hubble has transmitted incredibly detailed images of space, ⓑrevolutionizing our understanding of the universe. It has played a crucial role in facilitating pioneering discoveries about the relationships between celestial bodies, the formation of galaxies, and the expansion of the universe.
(A) It features a honeycomb-patterned mirror that is about three times ⓒlarge in diameter than Hubble’s round-shaped mirror, resulting in an image collection area that is 6.25 times wider. ⓓPositioned 1.5 million kilometers from Earth, Webb orbits the Sun alongside Earth, while Hubble orbits Earth itself.
(B) Moreover, its breathtaking images have sparked people’s imaginations and made space exploration an even more intriguing journey.
(C) To prepare for Hubble’s retirement, the James Webb Space Telescope was launched as its successor in 2021. Webb is a state-of-the-art space telescope with capabilities superior to those of any other telescope.
㉠또한 Webb은 적외선을 포착하는 것을 전문으로 하는데, 적외선은 Hubble에 의해 사용되는 가시광선보다 더 효과적으로 먼지가 많은 구역을 통과할 수 있다. These features enable Webb to offer a view of space with greatly ⓔenhanced clarity and minimal interference. As Webb continues its mission, it is expected to offer deeper insights into the birth of the universe and the evolutionary processes following the Big Bang.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: Hubble이 지구 대기권 상공에서 상세한 우주 이미지를 전송하며 천체 간의 관계, 은하의 형성, 우주의 팽창에 관한 선구적인 발견을 이끌어 우주에 대한 우리의 이해를 혁신적으로 변화시켰다는 주어진 글 다음에, Moreover(게다가)로 시작하여 Hubble의 추가적인 긍정적 역할로, Hubble이 전송한 이미지가 과학적 연구뿐만 아니라 사람들의 상상력을 자극하고 우주 탐사에 대한 대중의 흥미를 높이는 데에도 기여했다는 (B)가 가장 먼저 온다. 다음으로, Hubble의 퇴역에 대비하여 2021년에 후계자로 발사된 James Webb 우주 망원경을 소개하고, Webb이 다른 어떤 망원경보다 뛰어난 성능을 갖춘 최첨단 우주 망원경이라는 점을 설명하는 (C), 이어서 Webb을 It으로 지칭하여 그것의 뛰어난 기능을 설명하는 (A)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

body:
Thorough space exploration goes beyond remote observations and includes up-close examinations of celestial bodies, material collection, and on-site experiments. While human astronauts can be sent on these missions, it is often safer and more cost-effective to use robots. Robots can better withstand the harsh conditions of space, including extreme temperatures and high radiation levels that can pose serious risks to human astronauts.
A variety of robots have been developed for space missions. Some are designed to land on celestial bodies, while others are built for flyby missions. Some robots remain in fixed positions, while others are engineered for mobility. Robots also come in a range of shapes, resembling those of spacecraft, vehicles, or even humans. They are categorized and named according to their specific functions.

다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘이러한 발견은 과거 화성에 어떤 형태의 생명체가 존재했을지도 모른다는 가능성을 시사한다.’라는 뜻으로, These findings(이러한 발견들)가 앞서 언급된 발견들을 가리키므로 이 문장 앞에는 화성에 생명체가 존재했을 가능성을 뒷받침하는 발견에 관한 내용이 제시되어야 한다. (E) 앞에서 로봇형 차량인 로버의 예시로 제시된 Curiosity가 분화구 바닥에서 물줄기의 흔적을 발견하고 바위 가루에서 탄소와 같은 화학 물질을 확인했다고 했으므로, 이를 These findings(이러한 발견들)로 가리켜 과거 화성에 생명체가 존재했을 가능성을 언급하는 주어진 문장이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다. 따라서 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은 (E)이다.

body:
To prepare for Hubble’s retirement, the James Webb Space Telescope was launched as its successor in 2021. Webb is a state-of-the-art space telescope with capabilities superior to those of any other telescope. It features a honeycomb-patterned mirror that is about three times larger in diameter than Hubble’s round-shaped mirror, resulting in an image collection area that is 6.25 times wider. Positioned 1.5 million kilometers from Earth, Webb orbits the Sun alongside Earth, while Hubble orbits Earth itself. Webb also specializes in capturing infrared light, which can pass through dusty regions more effectively than the visible light used by Hubble. These features enable Webb to offer a view of space with greatly enhanced clarity and minimal interference. As Webb continues its mission, it is expected to offer deeper insights into the birth of the universe and the evolutionary processes following the Big Bang.

다음 글의 내용과 (A)~(E)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?
(A) Webb was launched to replace Hubble and continue space observations. (T/F)
(B) The smaller the mirror, the more advantageous it is for collecting images over a wider area. (T/F)
(C) Webb can observe distant objects through dust with less interference than Hubble. (T/F)
(D) Unlike Hubble, which travels around Earth, Webb moves around the Sun together with Earth. (T/F)
(E) Webb is expected to provide deeper insights into the events that occurred before the Big Bang. (T/F)
choices: T-F-T-T-F
T-F-T-F-T
F-F-T-F-T
T-F-F-F-T
T-T-F-F-T
solution:
차례대로 T-F-T-T-F이다.
(A) Webb는 Hubble을 대체하고 우주 관측을 계속하기 위해 발사되었다. (일치)
(B) 거울이 작을수록(→클수록) 더 넓은 지역에 걸쳐 이미지를 수집하는 데 더 유리하다. (불일치)
(C) Webb는 Hubble보다 방해를 덜 받으면서 먼지를 통과하여 멀리 있는 물체들을 관측할 수 있다. (일치)
(D) 지구 주위를 도는 Hubble과 달리, Webb은 지구와 함께 태양 주위를 돈다. (일치)
(E) Webb은 빅뱅 이전에(→이후에) 발생한 사건들에 대한 더 깊은 통찰을 제공할 것으로 기대된다. (불일치)

solution:

stationary 정지해 있는, 멈춰 있는

uniformity 동일성, 균일성
(C) 앞에서 망원경과 로봇이 은하, 행성, 천체의 아름다움과 신비를 밝혀 왔다고 설명하므로 기술이 발전함에 따라 우주의 비밀에 ‘더욱 가까워진’다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 closer to(더 가까이)가 적절하다.
farther from ~에서 더 먼

body:
Another widely recognized type of space robot is the rover, a robotic vehicle designed to move across the surface of planets and moons to explore their environments. Equipped with various scientific instruments, rovers conduct experiments and investigations while in motion, functioning like roaming laboratories. An iconic example is Curiosity, which landed on Mars in 2012. This car-sized rover made significant discoveries about Mars’s past. It found signs of a water stream on a crater’s floor and identified chemicals such as carbon in a powder sample drilled from a rock. These findings suggest the possibility that some form of life might have existed on Mars in the past.
While humanoid robots, which resemble humans in structure and movement, have not yet become common in space exploration, there have been significant advancements in this area as well. A humanoid robot named Robonaut 2 was sent to work on the International Space Station in 2011. Robonaut 2 was designed to assist astronauts in spacewalks and perform various tasks in dangerous environments. Despite their diversity, these robots share a common mission: to fearlessly venture into the unexplored territories of the universe.

오답
① 우주 로버는 왜 움직이는 실험실처럼 기능한다고 묘사되는가? (→다양한 과학 장비를 갖추고 있으며, 이동하면서 실험과 조사를 수행하기 때문이다.)
② Curiosity는 암석에서 채취한 가루 표본에서 무엇을 발견했는가? (→탄소와 같은 화학 물질을 발견했다.)
③ Curiosity의 발견은 과거 화성에 어떤 가능성이 있었음을 시사하는가? (→화성에 과거 어떤 형태의 생명체가 존재했을지도 모른다는 가능성을 시사한다.)
⑤ 우주 로봇들은 어떤 임무를 공통적으로 가지고 있는가? (→우주의 탐사되지 않은 영역을 두려움 없이 탐험하는 임무이다.)

위 담화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 것을 모두 고르면?
choices: We advise that you bring books
We suggest that you bring books
We demand that you bring books
We are sure that you will bring books
We guarantee that you will bring books
solution:
‘We recommend (that) ~‘은 ‘~을 추천한다’라는 의미로, 무엇을 제안하거나 권유할 때 쓰는 표현이다. 따라서 ① ‘We advise that you bring books(책을 가져올 것을 추천합니다)‘와 ② ’We suggest that you bring books(책을 가져올 것을 제안합니다)‘로 바꿔 쓸 수 있다.
오답

④ 책을 가져올 것이라고 확신합니다
⑤ 책을 가져올 것을 보장합니다

body:
On the first morning of their summer vacation, a young English boy named Jerry and his mother walked together towards their usual beach. But the young boy’s eyes followed the path to a rocky bay (A)[what / that] was a bit farther away. (B)[Feel / Feeling] that his attention was elsewhere, his mother worried about the ideas that he might be getting. The boy, noticing his mother’s concern, smiled at her and (C)[continued / continuing] following along. He kept glancing over his shoulder at the wild bay, however, imagining what it might hold.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: (A) that (B) Feeling (C) continued
(A) what (B) Feel (C) continued
(A) that (B) Feeling (C) continuing
(A) what (B) Feeling (C) continuing
(A) that (B) Feel (C) continued
solution:
(A) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(was a bit farther away)을 이끌어 명사구 a rocky bay를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 주격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다.
(B) 완전한 절(his mother ~ getting)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 연결되므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 his mother가 ‘느끼는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 Feeling이 적절하다.
(C) 주어 The boy에 이어지는 동사 smiled와 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되어야 하므로 과거형 동사 continued가 적절하다.

body:
Reaching the rocky bay, he started swimming but soon felt somewhat lonely being so far from his mother. After some time, he encountered a group of local boys who were diving from the rocks. They were around his age, and he desperately wanted to become friends with them. (A) He swam closer, and they turned to watch him. (B) One smiled and waved him over. (C) They showed him how to dive from the rocks into the deep water. (D) He tried diving with them, but he was too afraid. (E) Jerry tried calling out to them in the local language, “Bonjour! Merci! Monsieur, monsieur!” but they ignored him and swam away.
Noticing his hesitation, the boys soon lost interest.
윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘그의 망설임을 눈치채고 소년들은 곧 흥미를 잃었다.’라는 뜻으로 his hesitation(그의 망설임)이 쓰였으므로, 주어진 문장 앞에는 Jerry가 어떤 행동을 망설이거나 두려워하는 내용이 와야 한다. (D) 앞에서 소년들이 Jerry에게 바위에서 깊은 물속으로 다이빙하는 방법을 보여 주었다고 했고, (D)에서 Jerry가 소년들과 함께 다이빙을 시도했지만 너무 두려워했다고 했으므로, 바로 뒤에 Jerry의 망설임을 소년들이 알아차렸다는 내용의 주어진 문장이 자연스럽게 이어질 수 있다. 따라서 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은 (E)이다.

body:
Feeling rejected, Jerry watched the boys from a distance and noticed ⓐthat they were underwater for a long time. He started counting the seconds. At fifty, he started to worry. At one hundred, he wondered ⓑwhat he should yell for help. But around one hundred and fifty, he realized that they were in fact swimming through some rocks in the water and coming out the other side. After they left, he tried to do ⓒthat they had done, but when he tried to open his eyes ⓓto see underwater, his eyes stung from the salty water. With his eyes ⓔclosed, however, he was unable to see the tunnel that the boys had swum through. His only option was ⓕto give up and go home.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓑ what → whether 또는 if (뒤에 완전한 절(he ~ help)을 이끌어 ‘~인지 아닌지’의 의미로 동사 wondered의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌어야 하므로, what을 명사절 접속사 whether 또는 if로 고친다.)
*본문에는 whether가 쓰였음
ⓒ that → what (동사의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(they had done)을 이끌어, ‘~하는 것’이라는 뜻으로 do의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 that을 관계대명사 what으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 완전한 절(they ~ time)을 이끌어 동사 noticed의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that은 적절하다.
ⓓ 완전한 절(he tried ~ eyes)에 접속사 없이 이어지므로 준동사 자리이며, 흐름상 ‘물속을 보기 위해‘라는 목적의 의미를 나타내므로 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to see는 적절하다.
ⓔ 전치사 With, 명사구 his eyes와 함께 ’~하면서, ~한 채로‘의 의미를 갖는 ’with+명사(구)+분사‘ 구문을 이루고 있으며, his eyes가 ’감긴‘ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 closed는 적절하다.
ⓕ be동사 was에 이어지는 보어로 ’~하는 것‘의 의미를 갖는 명사적 용법의 to부정사 to give는 적절하다.

② 소년들이 물속에 계속 머무르자, Jerry는 점점 더 걱정하게 되었고 도움 요청을 고려했다.

body:
Back home that evening, Jerry asked his mother for swimming goggles. After receiving them the next day, he ran off back to the bay. Underwater, he was now able to see the tunnel clearly. He tried to enter it, but the darkness and the feeling of seaweed on his skin frightened him. He gave up and decided to practice holding his breath underwater instead.
From that day forward, every morning, the boy left his mother at the beach and came to the rocks to practice his breathing and diving. Some days, he pushed himself too hard, and his nose would bleed from too much practice. His mother told him that she was worried about him and ______. But the beach looked different to him now. It now seemed like a place for small children.
윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: let him spend as much time as possible at the bay
encouraged him to explore the dangerous tunnel
forbade him from going swimming in any water
taught him how to breathe underwater safely
had him join her at their usual beach
solution:

body:
The next morning, Jerry’s mother asked him if he was interested in trying another beach. He first answered no, regretting that he had made his mother think that he was bored with their usual place. As they were walking, however, he suddenly changed his mind and said, “I’d like to go and have a look at those rocks down there.” She gave the idea some thought. The area he was pointing to looked somewhat dangerous, but she decided it would be fine to let him go on his own. As his mother walked away, Jerry felt like running after her again and enjoying the beach as they had always done, but he did not.
Reaching the rocky bay, he started swimming but soon felt somewhat lonely being so far from his mother. After some time, he encountered a group of local boys who were diving from the rocks. They were around his age, and he desperately wanted to become friends with them. He swam closer, and they turned to watch him. One smiled and waved him over. They showed him how to dive from the rocks into the deep water. He tried diving with them, but he was too afraid. Noticing his hesitation, the boys soon lost interest. Jerry tried calling out to them in the local language, “Bonjour! Merci! Monsieur, monsieur!” but they ignored him and swam away.
윗글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: What did Jerry regret after his mother's question?
Why did Jerry’s mother hesitate to allow him to head toward the rocky area?
Why did Jerry’s mother think it was all right for him to go alone?
What was Jerry eager to do when he encountered local boys around his age?
Why did the local boys eventually lose interest in Jerry?
solution:
Jerry가 가리킨 바위가 많은 지역이 다소 위험해 보인다고 생각했음에도 불구하고 그가 혼자 가도록 두어도 괜찮을 것이라고 결정했다고만 언급되었을 뿐 그 이유는 언급된 바가 없으므로, ③ ‘Jerry의 어머니는 왜 그가 혼자 가도 괜찮다고 생각했는가?‘는 답할 수 없는 질문이다.
오답
① Jerry는 어머니의 질문 이후에 무엇을 후회했는가? (→ 그들이 평소 가던 곳에 싫증이 났다고 어머니가 생각하게 만든 것 같아서 후회했다.)
② Jerry의 어머니는 왜 그가 바위투성이의 지역으로 가는 것을 허락하는 것을 망설였는가? (→Jerry가 가리킨 지역이 다소 위험해 보였기 때문이다.)
④ Jerry는 자신과 또래인 현지 소년들과 마주쳤을 때 무엇을 간절히 하고 싶어 했는가? (→ 그는 그들과 몹시 친구가 되고 싶었다.)
⑤ 현지 소년들은 결국 왜 Jerry에게 흥미를 잃었는가? (→ Jerry가 두려움 때문에 그들과 함께 다이빙하지 못하자 그의 망설임을 눈치 채고 곧 흥미를 잃었다.)

body:
Back home that evening, Jerry asked his mother for swimming goggles. After receiving them the next day, he ran off back to the bay. Underwater, he was now able to see the tunnel clearly. He tried to enter it, but the darkness and the feeling of seaweed on his skin frightened him. He (A)[gave up / persisted] and decided to practice ⓐholding his breath underwater instead.
From that day forward, every morning, the boy left his mother at the beach and came to the rocks ⓑto practice his breathing and diving. Some days, he pushed himself too hard, and his nose would bleed from too much practice. His mother told him that she was (B)[worried about / proud of] him and had him ⓒjoin her at their usual beach. But the beach looked different to him now. It now seemed like a place for small children.
Jerry soon began to feel (C)[calm / restless] being back at the beach with his mother, and he worried that all the practice he ⓓhad put in would go to waste. The next day, he decided to go back to the rocky bay. He now spent his days exploring the tunnel at the bay and practicing his breathing whenever he was back with his mother. He knew that being prepared would help him ⓔconquering the tunnel that had defeated him.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓔ conquering → conquer 또는 to conquer (동사 help, 목적어 him에 이어지는 목적격보어 자리로, 동사 help는 ‘help+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형/to부정사)’의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이므로 conquering을 동사원형 conquer 또는 to부정사 to conquer로 고친다.)
*본문에서는 conquer가 쓰였음
오답
ⓐ 동사 practice는 동명사를 목적어로 취하는 동사이므로 동명사 holding은 적절하다.
ⓑ 완전한 절(the boy ~ rocks)에 접속사 없이 이어지므로 준동사 자리이며, 흐름상 ‘호흡과 다이빙을 연습하기 위해’라는 목적의 의미를 나타내므로 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to practice는 적절하다.
ⓒ 동사 had가 ‘~하게 하다’라는 뜻의 사역동사로 쓰일 때 ‘have+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형/과거분사)’의 구조로 쓰이며, 목적어와 목적격보어가 능동 관계일 때 동사원형, 수동 관계일 때 과거분사를 쓴다. 여기서 목적어 him이 ‘함께하는’ 주체이므로, 목적격보어 자리에 능동을 나타내는 동사원형 join이 쓰인 것은 적절하다.
ⓓ 주절의 걱정한(worried) 시점보다 연습했던 상황이 더 먼저 발생한 일이므로 과거보다 앞선 시제를 나타내는 과거완료 had put은 적절하다.

Last Stop on Market Street is a great example. It is a popular book by Matt de la Peña and Christian Robinson. It follows a boy named CJ who learns to appreciate everyday beauty on a bus ride. He soon found the entrance to the tunnel. He took the edges of the hole in his hands and drew (A)[him / himself] into it. It was pitch black, but he kept counting, just as he had practiced. Fifty, fifty-one, fifty-two… Soon he reached a hundred, a hundred and one… He kept moving through the tunnel, and when he thought he couldn’t last any longer, he spotted a crack of light at the end. The feeling of victory filled him as he realized that with a few more strokes, he would be coming out the other side. He felt like he was running out of air, but he kept kicking and thinking just a little bit more!

He had made it. After resting a short while on the warm rock, he got on his feet and walked back home. His mother’s eyes lit up, as she was happy (B)[seeing / to see] him back. “Did you have a nice morning?” she asked. Jerry replied with pride, “Mom, I can stay underwater for two minutes, three minutes, at least!” His mom thought about telling him (C)[to rest / resting] for the remainder of the day, but she didn’t have to. He was now happy to stay home and rest. Going to the bay was no longer important to him.

Reaching the rocky bay, he started swimming but soon felt somewhat lonely being so far from his mother. After some time, he encountered a group of local boys who were diving from the rocks. They were around his age, and he desperately wanted to become friends with them. He swam closer, and they turned to watch him. One smiled and waved him over. They showed him how to dive from the rocks into the deep water. He tried diving with them, but he was too afraid. Noticing his hesitation, the boys soon lost interest. Jerry tried calling out to them in the local language, “Bonjour! Merci! Monsieur, monsieur!” but they ignored him and swam away.

Feeling rejected, Jerry watched the boys from a distance and noticed that they were underwater for a long time. He started counting the seconds. At fifty, he started to worry. At one hundred, he wondered whether he should yell for help. But around one hundred and fifty, he realized that they were in fact swimming through some rocks in the water and coming out the other side. After they left, he tried to do what they had done, but when he tried to open his eyes to see underwater, his eyes stung from the salty water. With his eyes closed, however, he was unable to see the tunnel that the boys had swum through. His only option was to give up and go home.

Jerry approached the local boys in the hope of making friends, but they became (A)______ to him when he was too frightened to dive with them; afterward, he discovered that they were swimming through an underwater tunnel but gave up trying to (B)______ them because of the pain caused by the salty water.

다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

(A) (B)
choices: indifferent / help
hospitable / imitate
indifferent / copy
hospitable / follow
friendly / assist
solution:
요약문 Jerry는 현지 소년들과 친구가 되기를 바라며 다가갔지만, 너무 두려워 그들과 함께 다이빙하지 못하자 그들은 그에게 (A)무관심해졌다; 이후 그는 소년들이 수중 터널을 통과해 헤엄치고 있다는 사실을 발견했지만, 소금물로 인한 고통 때문에 소년들을 (B)따라 하려는 시도를 포기했다.

① 무관심한 / 돕다
② 환대하는, 친절한 / 따라하다
④ 환대하는, 친절한 / 따라 가다
⑤ 친절한, 우호적인 / 돕다

body:
G: Daehun, did you know that sunsets on Mars are different from those on Earth?
B: Really? You mean they’re not red and orange?
G: That’s right, they aren’t. Sunsets are somewhat blue on Mars.
B: Wow! Why is that?
G: It’s because of the Martian atmosphere. Unlike Earth’s atmosphere, it’s full of large dust particles.
B: How does that affect the sunset colors?
G: When the sun sets on Mars, these particles filter out the red light from the sun and allow only the blue light to reach our eyes.
B: Oh, that’s really surprising!
G: Plus, the sky on Mercury would look black during the day because the planet has virtually no atmosphere.
B: Interesting! I’m surprised to learn that each planet has such unique features.

choices: Sunsets on Earth are generally red or orange.
The Martian atmosphere is full of large dust particles.
The dust particles in Mars’s atmosphere make its sunsets appear blue.
The light from the sun includes both red and blue light.
Mercury’s atmosphere blocks the red light coming from the sun.

M: It’s shiny and blue, as always.

ⓐ Unbelievable! Why did you want to become an astronaut?
ⓑ I do plant growth experiments. I’ve been growing vegetables such as tomatoes and peppers here.
ⓒ I’ve always been interested in how plants grow in space.

M: Scientific knowledge is essential, but physical and mental health are just as important.

body:
[1]
When we observe space from the ground, Earth’s atmosphere creates obstacles for our vision. It absorbs specific types of lights such as ultraviolet and infrared, causing distortions in our observations and making some objects beyond the atmosphere invisible. Consequently, the space we see from Earth’s surface can differ significantly from its actual appearance. To overcome these limitations, telescopes are launched into space beyond Earth’s atmosphere.
Space telescopes are specifically designed to capture a spectrum of light that is not visible on Earth. This capability provides us with a clear and uninterrupted view of celestial objects, allowing us to better observe stars, black holes, and galaxies located billions of light years away from Earth. The data and images gathered by space telescopes are invaluable to scientists, ⓐenabling them to study the birth and death of celestial bodies and their unique characteristics.
[2]
Thorough space exploration goes beyond remote observations and includes up-close examinations of celestial bodies, material collection, and on-site experiments. While human astronauts can be sent on these missions, it is often safer and more cost-effective ⓑuse robots. Robots can better withstand the harsh conditions of space, including extreme temperatures and high radiation levels ⓒthat can pose serious risks to human astronauts.
A variety of robots have ⓓbeen developed for space missions. Some are designed to land on celestial bodies, while others are built for flyby missions. Some robots remain in fixed positions, while others are engineered for mobility. Robots also come in a range of shapes, ⓔresembling those of spacecraft, vehicles, or even humans. They are categorized and named according to their specific functions.

body:
Among the various space telescopes in operation, the Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990, stands out as an ⓐunprecedented achievement in space technology. Orbiting approximately 600 kilometers above Earth’s atmosphere, Hubble has transmitted incredibly detailed images of space, ⓑrevolutionizing our understanding of the universe. It has played a crucial role in facilitating pioneering discoveries about the relationships between celestial bodies, the formation of galaxies, and the expansion of the universe. Moreover, its breathtaking images have ⓒsparked people’s imaginations and made space exploration an even more intriguing journey.
To prepare for Hubble’s retirement, the James Webb Space Telescope was launched as its ⓓsuccessor in 2021. Webb is a ⓔstate-of-the-art space telescope with capabilities superior to those of any other telescope. It features a honeycomb-patterned mirror that is about three times larger in diameter than Hubble’s round-shaped mirror, resulting in an image collection area that is 6.25 times wider. (A)Webb은 지구로부터 150만 킬로미터 떨어진 지점에 위치하면서 지구와 나란히 태양의 궤도를 도는 반면, Hubble은 지구 자체의 궤도를 돈다. Webb also specializes in capturing infrared light, which can pass through dusty regions more effectively than the visible light used by Hubble. These features enable Webb to offer a view of space with greatly enhanced clarity and minimal interference. As Webb continues its mission, it is expected to offer deeper insights into the birth of the universe and the evolutionary processes following the Big Bang.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: how early astronomers contributed to the development of modern space exploration
the advancement of space exploration through a new generation of space telescopes
how infrared technology helps scientists observe distant regions of the universe
reasons the Hubble Space Telescope failed to make meaningful discoveries
how ground-based and space telescopes differ in collecting data
