[1]
Probes are one notable type of space robots. These spacecraft-like robots are designed to capture photos and gather data without needing to land on celestial bodies. For example, the twin Voyagers launched in 1977 are historic probes. These probes successfully flew by the major outer planets of our solar system — Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune — (A)[discovered / discovering] numerous fascinating details about them. One of the Voyagers’ significant findings was the presence of highly active volcanoes on Io, one of Jupiter’s moons, marking the first evidence of geological processes observed on other planets. After completing their planetary missions, these probes continued their journey beyond our solar system. Voyager 1 first entered interstellar space in 2012 and became the farthest human-made object from Earth.
[2]
Another widely recognized type of space robot is the rover, a robotic vehicle (B)[designed / was designed] to move across the surface of planets and moons to explore their environments. Equipped with various scientific instruments, rovers conduct experiments and investigations while in motion, functioning like roaming laboratories. An iconic example is Curiosity, (C)[which / where] landed on Mars in 2012. This car-sized rover made significant discoveries about Mars’s past. It found signs of a water stream on a crater’s floor and identified chemicals such as carbon in a powder sample drilled from a rock. ⓐ이러한 발견들은 과거 화성에 어떤 형태의 생명체가 존재했을지도 모른다는 가능성을 시사한다.

body:
[1]
Since ancient times, we have looked to the sky with wonder, ⓐcurious about what lies beyond our world. This inherent desire to explore the universe has encouraged technological innovations that can aid us in this pursuit. Among these advancements are space telescopes and space robots, which ⓑhave paved the way for our journey toward understanding the mysteries of space.
[2]
When we observe space from the ground, Earth’s atmosphere creates obstacles for our vision. It absorbs specific types of lights such as ultraviolet and infrared, causing distortions in our observations and making some objects beyond the atmosphere invisible. Consequently, the space we see from Earth’s surface can differ significantly from its actual appearance. To overcome these limitations, telescopes are launched into space beyond Earth’s atmosphere.
Space telescopes are specifically designed to capture a spectrum of light that is not visible on Earth. This capability provides us with a clear and uninterrupted view of celestial objects, allowing us to better observe stars, black holes, and galaxies ⓒlocate billions of light years away from Earth. The data and images gathered by space telescopes are invaluable to scientists, enabling them to study the birth and death of celestial bodies and their unique characteristics.
Among the various space telescopes in operation, the Hubble Space Telescope, launched in 1990, stands out as an unprecedented achievement in space technology. ⓓOrbited approximately 600 kilometers above Earth’s atmosphere, Hubble has transmitted incredibly detailed images of space, revolutionizing our understanding of the universe. It has played a crucial role in facilitating pioneering discoveries about the relationships between celestial bodies, the formation of galaxies, and the expansion of the universe. Moreover, its breathtaking images have sparked people’s imaginations and made space exploration an even ⓔmore intriguing journey.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓒ locate → located
(명사구 stars, black holes, and galaxies(별과 블랙홀, 은하)를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, locate는 ‘위치하다, 위치시키다’라는 뜻의 타동사로 수식을 받는 대상인 수식을 받는 stars, black holes, and galaxies가 ‘위치한’ 대상이므로 locate는 수동의 의미인 과거분사 located로 고친다.)
ⓓ Orbited → Orbiting
(완전한 절(Hubble ~ space) 앞에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 연결되므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 Hubble이 ‘궤도를 그리며 도는’ 주체이며, orbit이 ‘궤도를 돌다’라는 뜻의 자동사로 쓰였으므로 Orbited는 능동의 의미를 나타내는 현재분사 Orbiting으로 고친다.)

To prepare for Hubble’s retirement, the James Webb Space Telescope was launched as its successor in 2021. Webb is a state-of-the-art space telescope with capabilities superior to those of any other telescope. It features a honeycomb-patterned mirror that is about three times larger in diameter than Hubble’s round-shaped mirror, resulting in an image collection area that is 6.25 times wider. Positioned 1.5 million kilometers from Earth, Webb orbits the Sun alongside Earth, while Hubble orbits Earth itself. Webb also specializes in capturing infrared light, which can pass through dusty regions more effectively than the visible light used by Hubble. These features enable Webb to ______. As Webb continues its mission, it is expected to offer deeper insights into the birth of the universe and the evolutionary processes following the Big Bang.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: determine the exact age of individual stars
provide clearer views with minimal interference
collect visible light from distant celestial objects
capture images of larger areas of Earth’s surface
detect changes in the orbits of distant celestial objects
solution: Webb의 거울은 Hubble보다 지름이 약 세 배 크고 이미지 수집 면적도 6.25배 넓으며, Hubble이 사용하는 가시광선보다 먼지가 많은 영역을 더 효과적으로 통과하는 적외선을 포착하는 데 특화되었다고 했으므로, 이러한 특징을 통해 천체를 더 뚜렷하게 관측할 수 있다는 내용이 이어져야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ❷ ‘방해를 최소화하면서 더 선명한 시야를 제공하다‘가 적절하다.

body:
A variety of robots have been developed for space missions. Some are designed to land on celestial bodies, while others are built for flyby missions. Some robots remain in fixed positions, while others are engineered for (A)[mobility / immobility]. Robots also come in a range of shapes, resembling those of spacecraft, vehicles, or even humans. They are categorized and named according to their specific functions.
Probes are one notable type of space robots. These spacecraft-like robots are designed to capture photos and gather data without needing to land on celestial bodies. For example, the twin Voyagers launched in 1977 are historic probes. These probes successfully flew by the major outer planets of our solar system — Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune — discovering numerous fascinating details about them. One of the Voyagers’ significant findings was the (B)[presence / absence] of highly active volcanoes on Io, one of Jupiter’s moons, marking the first evidence of geological processes observed on other planets. After completing their planetary missions, these probes continued their journey beyond our solar system. Voyager 1 first entered interstellar space in 2012 and became the farthest human-made object from Earth.
As we journey through the vast universe, telescopes and robots have been our eyes and hands. Their lenses and sensors (C)[obscure / reveal] the beauty and mysteries of galaxies, planets, and celestial wonders. As technology advances, we find ourselves closer to the secrets of the universe than ever before. The future of space exploration promises wonders beyond our imagination, and this fills us with great excitement.
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: mobility presence obscure
immobility absence obscure
immobility presence reveal
mobility presence reveal
mobility absence reveal
solution:
(A) 다양한 로봇들의 특징을 설명하는 부분으로 일부 로봇들은 고정된 위치에 머무른다는 내용과 역접의 접속사인 while로 연결되어 있으므로 다른 로봇들은 이동할 수 있다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 mobility(이동성)가 적절하다.
immobility 부동성
(B) 뒤에서 Io의 활발한 화산이 다른 행성에서 관찰된 지질학적 과정의 최초 증거가 되었다고 설명하므로 활화산들이 ‘존재’한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 presence(존재)가 적절하다.
absence 부재
(C) 앞에서 망원경과 로봇의 렌즈와 센서가 우주 탐사에서 인간의 눈과 손 역할을 하며, 뒤에서 우주의 비밀에 더욱 가까워졌다고 설명하므로 우주의 아름다움과 신비를 ‘드러내다’는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 reveal(~을 드러내다)이 적절하다.
obscure ~을 덮어 가리다

G: Daehun, did you know that sunsets on Mars are different from those on Earth?
B: Really? You mean they’re not red and orange?
G: That’s right, they aren’t. Sunsets are somewhat blue on Mars.
B: Wow! Why is that?

To prepare for Hubble’s retirement, the James Webb Space Telescope was launched as its successor in 2021. Webb is a state-of-the-art space telescope with capabilities superior to those of any other telescope. It features a honeycomb-patterned mirror that is about three times larger in diameter than Hubble’s round-shaped mirror, resulting in an image collection area that is 6.25 times wider. Positioned 1.5 million kilometers from Earth, Webb orbits the Sun alongside Earth, while Hubble orbits Earth itself. Webb also specializes in capturing infrared light, which can pass through dusty regions more effectively than the visible light used by Hubble. These features enable Webb to offer a view of space with greatly enhanced clarity and minimal interference. As Webb continues its mission, it is expected to offer deeper insights into the birth of the universe and the evolutionary processes following the Big Bang.

the enhancement of astronomical observations through Webb's advanced technology

body:
Probes are one notable type of space robots. These spacecraft-like robots are designed to capture photos and gather data without needing to land on celestial bodies. For example, the twin Voyagers ⓐlaunched in 1977 are historic probes. These probes successfully flew by the major outer planets of our solar system — Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune — discovering numerous fascinating details about them. One of the Voyagers’ significant findings was the presence of highly active volcanoes on Io, one of Jupiter’s moons, ⓑmarking the first evidence of geological processes observed on other planets. After completing their planetary missions, these probes continued their journey beyond our solar system. Voyager 1 first entered interstellar space in 2012 and became the farthest human-made object from Earth.
Another widely recognized type of space robot is the rover, a robotic vehicle designed to move across the surface of planets and moons to explore their environments. ⓒEquipped with various scientific instruments, rovers conduct experiments and investigations while in motion, functioning like roaming laboratories. An iconic example is Curiosity, ⓓwhich landed on Mars in 2012. This car-sized rover made significant discoveries about Mars’s past. It found signs of a water stream on a crater’s floor and identified chemicals such as carbon in a powder sample drilled from a rock. These findings suggest the possibility ⓔwhich some form of life might have existed on Mars in the past.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

ⓔ which → that (완전한 절(some ~ past)을 이끌어 앞의 추상 명사구 the possibility를 부연 설명하는 동격의 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 which를 동격 접속사 that으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 뒤에 동사 are가 있으므로 주어 the twin Voyagers(쌍둥이 탐사선)를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, 수식을 받는 the twin Voyagers가 ‘발사된’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미인 과거분사 launched는 적절하다.
ⓑ 완전한 절(One ~ Io)과 Io를 부연 설명하는 동격의 명사구 one of Jupiter’s moons 뒤에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 앞 절의 내용이 ‘나타내는’ 주체이며 뒤에 목적어인 명사구 the first ~ planets가 이어지므로 능동의 의미인 현재분사 marking은 적절하다.
ⓒ 콤마(,) 뒤의 완전한 절(rovers ~ motion)과 접속사 없이 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 rovers가, ‘equip A with B(A에 B를 갖추다)’의 대상이므로 수동 표현인 ‘A be equipped with B‘를 이루는 과거분사 Equipped는 적절하다.

A variety of robots have been developed for space missions. Some are designed to land on celestial bodies, while others are built for flyby missions. Some robots remain in fixed positions, while others are engineered for mobility.
(A) For example, the twin Voyagers launched in 1977 are historic probes. These probes successfully flew by the major outer planets of our solar system — Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune — discovering numerous fascinating details about them.
(B) Probes are one notable type of space robots. These spacecraft-like robots are designed to capture photos and gather data without needing to land on celestial bodies.
(C) Robots also come in a range of shapes, resembling those of spacecraft, vehicles, or even humans. They are categorized and named according to their specific functions.
One of the Voyagers’ significant findings was the presence of highly active volcanoes on Io, one of Jupiter’s moons, marking the first evidence of geological processes observed on other planets. After completing their planetary missions, these probes continued their journey beyond our solar system. Voyager 1 first entered interstellar space in 2012 and became the farthest human-made object from Earth.

solution: 친구가 파티에 초대하지만 참석하고 싶지 않아 거절할 핑계를 대거나, 마음에 들지 않는 선물을 받고도 친구들을 실망시키지 않기 위해 좋아하는 척한다는 주어진 글 뒤에 앞선 두 가지 상황들을 These situations(이러한 상황들)로 이어받아, 이것이 선의의 거짓말에 관한 윤리적 딜레마임을 설명하는 (C), 사람들이 관계에 해를 끼치는 것을 피하기 위해 선의의 거짓말을 한다는 마지막 문장에 이어, 거짓말을 하는 것은 도덕적으로 잘못된 것 아니냐는 질문과 함께 거짓말은 어떤 상황에서도 도덕적으로 그르다는 Immanuel Kant의 주장을 소개하는 (B), In contrast(그와 반대로)를 통해 Immanuel Kant의 주장과 반대되는, 거짓말이 전체적인 행복을 증가시킨다면 도덕적으로 허용될 수 있다는 John Stuart Mill의 주장을 소개하는 (A)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

Online education is definitely superior to traditional education. ⓐLiving in an era in which we enjoy technical innovations and boundless connectivity, we should take advantage of ⓑwhat is available in education as well. For instance, take Khan Academy, an online education program ⓓprovides free lectures. It started when its founder, Sal Khan, uploaded teaching videos he made for his cousin who was living far away. Now learners from all around the world can enjoy the program’s outstanding lectures on a wide variety of subjects at any time they want.
[2]
“Teaching and learning is the relationship between teachers and students,” Larry Cuban, an education expert from Stanford University, once explained. No matter ⓔwhat advanced technology it is equipped with, it is undeniable that online education focuses mainly on delivering information. It overlooks that education is deeply rooted in the teacher-student relationship, which traditional education is based on. The following will demonstrate the strengths of traditional education in contrast to online education.
First, traditional education has proven more successful in providing an educational environment where students can concentrate and learn better. According to a study on students’ level of concentration and understanding in traditional classrooms and online classes, students in traditional classrooms performed better. solution:
(A) 완전한 절(it ~ students)을 이끌어 be동사 is에 이어지는 주격보어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 명사절 접속사 that이 알맞다.
(B) 주어 each learner가 개인화된 온라인 수업을 ‘받는’ 대상이므로 단수로 수일치한 수동태(be+p.p.) is offered가 알맞다. 참고로 동사 offer는 ‘offer+간접목적어+직접목적어’의 구조로 두 개의 목적어를 취하는 4형식 동사이므로 수동태(be+p.p.)로 전환될 때, 뒤에 나머지 목적어인 명사(구)가 이어진다.
(C) 접속사 when 뒤에 분사구문을 이루는 being이 생략된 형태로 ‘접속사+보어’를 이루는 구문, 또는 접속사 when 뒤에 ‘주어+be동사’인 they are이 생략된 부사절 축약으로 볼 수 있으므로, when 뒤에는 보어로 올 수 있는 형용사 necessary가 알맞다.

body:
by Emily Mitchell, Editor
In Isaac Asimov’s short story The Fun They Had, a young girl named Margie living in 2155 receives her education through a “mechanical teacher.” Her learning takes place one-on-one in her study next to her bedroom. One day, she finds a “real” book on traditional schools from hundreds of years ago and longs to receive a traditional education. She dreams of attending a real school where all the students learn the same things, laugh and play on the playground, and go home together at the end of the day.
Margie’s desire reflects the ongoing debate on the merits of online education compared to those of traditional education. As many of us already know, online education is instruction in electronically supported learning environments using multimedia and Internet platforms. Traditional education, on the other hand, generally refers to the conventional teaching-learning process in a classroom setting in which teachers and students are present together.
다음 글의 내용과 (A)~(E)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?
(A) Margie learns alone at home with the help of a computer-like teacher. (T/F)
(B) After discovering an old book, Margie becomes interested in attending a school where students spend time together. (T/F)
(C) Margie wishes she could attend a real school, studying different subjects individually in the same classroom. (T/F)
(D) Online education uses digital tools and the Internet to teach students. (T/F)
(E) Traditional education generally involves teachers and students being together in a classroom as part of the teaching and learning process. (T/F)
choices: T-T-T-T-T
T-F-T-T-F
F-T-T-F-T
T-T-F-F-T
T-T-F-T-T
solution:
차례대로 T-T-F-T-T이다.
(A) Margie는 컴퓨터와 같은 교사의 도움을 받아 집에서 혼자 학습한다. (일치)
(B) 오래된 책을 발견한 후, Margie는 학생들이 함께 시간을 보내는 학교에 다니는 것에 관심을 갖게 된다. (일치)
(C) Margie는 학생들이 같은 교실에서 서로 다른 과목을 개별적으로(→모두 같은 과목을 함께) 공부하는 실제 학교에 다닐 수 있기를 바란다. (불일치)
(D) 온라인 교육은 학생들을 가르치기 위해 디지털 도구와 인터넷을 사용한다. (일치)
(E) 전통적 교육은 일반적으로 교수와 학습 과정의 일부로 교사와 학생들이 교실에서 함께 있는 것을 포함한다. (일치)

While White Ox is his most recognized piece, much of his work ⓐdealt with the themes of young children and family. Lee used common objects such as animals and children to produce artwork (A)[what / that] reminded him of “home.”
This painting, Two Children and Fish and Crab, seems ⓑlighthearted at first glance. However, behind this seemingly happy image of children (B)[is / are] a sad story. In 1951, Lee and his family took ⓒrefuge on Jejudo. Although they were ⓓfleeing from the war, for Lee, the year that he spent on the island with his wife and children was the highlight of his life. Sadly, it was also the last year of happiness for his family. Poverty from the war led to the ⓔseparation of his family, as he was forced to send his wife and two sons to Japan for a better chance of survival. During this time of separation, Lee continued to create art, (C)[which / that] was his way of remembering the memories he had with his family.

<보기>
ⓐ deal with: to do business with someone or have a business connection with someone

body:
Alfonse Mucha
Finding the light at the end of the long tunnel
(A)Alfonse Mucha(1860-1939)는 최초의 아르 누보 예술가들 중 한 명이었으며, 이것이 이러한 형태의 예술이 ‘Mucha 양식’이라고 불리는 것으로 이어졌다.
His style became famous later on in his life and is used often, even to this day. His fame, however, did not happen overnight.
As a younger artist, Mucha was rejected when he applied for his local art school, but he did not give up. Holding on to his dream of one day becoming an artist, he moved to Vienna at the age of 19 to continue his education. After working different jobs to support himself during his studies, he finally finished his schooling and 7 years later, moved to Paris.
In Paris, Mucha made money drawing inserts and illustrations for magazines but also continued working on his own art. His big break came much later in 1894, ⓐwhich he landed the opportunity to draw a poster for the play Gismonda. He was working alone late on Christmas Eve when he was commissioned to produce a drawing of the actor Sarah Bernhardt for a poster of the play. Based on a style that he had been developing, ⓑhe produced a life-sized poster, portrayed Bernhardt as a member of Byzantine royalty. This led him to eventually become known as a primary figure in the development of the Art Nouveau form.
Mucha was not an instant success when he started his career, but he kept working on his own style until the right opportunity came along. Success is said to happen only (B)______, and Mucha’s story reminds us that beautiful things can happen when the two finally come together.

윗글의 빈칸 (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: when talent replaces patient effort
when preparation meets opportunity
when people put their thoughts into action
when recognition comes before years of practice
when financial support enables people to pursue their passions
solution:
앞에서 Mucha는 미술 학교에서 거절당했지만 포기하지 않고 노력했으며, 자신의 꿈을 이루기 위해 계속해서 교육을 받고, 파리에서도 다른 일을 하면서 자신의 예술 활동을 이어 가며 자신만의 스타일을 계속 발전시켰고, 마침내 Gismonda 포스터를 그릴 기회를 얻었다고 했다. 그리고 이러한 과정을 빈칸 앞 문장에서 Mucha가 처음에는 성공하지 못했지만, 적절한 기회가 올 때까지 자신만의 양식을 계속 발전시켰다고 말하고 있으며, 뒤에 이어지는 문장에서 빈칸에 언급된 것을 the two로 받아 ‘마침내 그 두 가지가 결합할 때‘라고 말하고 있으므로, 성공은 준비가 기회와 만날 때 이루어진다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ② ‘준비가 기회와 만날 때’가 적절하다.

① 재능이 인내심 있는 노력을 대신할 때
③ 사람들이 자신의 생각을 행동으로 옮길 때
④ 수년간의 연습보다 인정이 먼저 찾아올 때
⑤ 재정적 지원이 사람들이 자신의 열정을 추구할 수 있게 할 때

Lee Jungseop
Hope within life difficulties
Lee Jungseop (1916-1956) is one of the most important artists of 20th century Korean modern art. While White Ox is his most recognized piece, much of his work dealt with the themes of young children and family. Lee used common objects such as animals and children to produce artwork that reminded him of “home.”
This painting, Two Children and Fish and Crab, seems lighthearted at first glance.
(A) Although they were fleeing from the war, for Lee, the year that he spent on the island with his wife and children was the highlight of his life. Sadly, it was also the last year of happiness for his family.
(B) Poverty from the war led to the separation of his family, as he was forced to send his wife and two sons to Japan for a better chance of survival.
(C) However, behind this seemingly happy image of children is a sad story. In 1951, Lee and his family took refuge on Jejudo.
During this time of separation, Lee continued to create art, which was his way of remembering the memories he had with his family.
Underneath the cheerful content of the painting is the sadness that Lee felt as he lived alone, far away from his family. But these paintings also allowed him to remember the good times and look forward to a happier future. His ability to express this hope through art brought his work much attention, and his art is a source of comfort to people to this day.

At the Well. This painting, with its warm colors and detailed portrayal of an (A)[ordinary / unusual] day on a farm, fills the viewer with a sense of calm. In this depiction of another peaceful day, we see farmers go about their day — sweeping, pushing a cart, and drawing water out of the well. We can also see cows and goats grazing on the grass, alongside the farmers. This painting was done by Anna Mary Robertson Moses (1860-1961), better known as Grandma Moses, one of the most well-known figures in the world of Naive art.
Before she started painting, Grandma Moses lived on a farm, selling homemade foods at local markets while raising her five children. She started painting in her 70s but had become an internationally recognized artist by the time she passed away at the age of 101. During that time, she produced more than 1,600 paintings. These paintings portray a simple lifestyle in the rural countryside, bringing about a sense of nostalgia about the past.
Her first paintings were done with leftover crayons and old paintbrushes that had been used by her grandchildren. She started by making these paintings to give away as gifts. Later, she tried selling them at local markets, but they received little or no attention. Then, one day in 1939, an art collector named Louis Calder (B)[overlooked / noticed] her paintings in the window of a drugstore. Realizing the beauty of her work, he organized exhibitions of her drawings, which were all a big hit with the public, and the rest is history. The exhibitions brought the work of Grandma Moses to the public, allowing people from all walks of life to appreciate the calming beauty of her everyday life. The story of Grandma Moses is a reminder that it is never too late to (C)[accomplish / give up] our dreams.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: unusual / overlooked / accomplish
ordinary / noticed / give up
ordinary / noticed / accomplish
unusual / noticed / accomplish
ordinary / overlooked / give up
solution:
(A) 뒤에서 농부들이 쓸고, 수레를 밀고, 우물에서 물을 긷는 등 농장의 일상적인 모습들을 묘사하고 있으므로 평범한 하루라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ordinary(평범한)가 적절하다.
unusual 특이한
(B) 뒤에서 그(=Louis Calder)가 그녀 작품의 아름다움을 깨닫고 그녀의 그림 전시회를 열었다고 했으므로, 약국 창문에 걸린 그녀의 그림을 발견했다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 noticed(~을 알아채다, 발견하다)가 적절하다.
overlook ~을 못 보고 넘어가다
(C) 앞에서 Grandma Moses는 70대라는 늦은 나이에 그림을 시작하여 101세의 나이로 세상을 떠날 무렵에는 국제적으로 인정받는 예술가가 되었다고 했으므로 꿈을 이루기에 결코 너무 늦은 때는 없다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 accomplish(~을 이루다)가 적절하다.
give ~ up ~을 포기하다

body:
As a younger artist, Mucha was rejected when he applied for his local art school, but he did not give up. Holding on to his dream of one day becoming an artist, he moved to Vienna at the age of 19 to continue his education. After working different jobs to support himself during his studies, he finally finished his schooling and 7 years later, moved to Paris.
In Paris, Mucha made money drawing inserts and illustrations for magazines but also continued working on his own art. His big break came much later in 1894, when he landed the opportunity to draw a poster for the play Gismonda. He was working alone late on Christmas Eve when he was commissioned to produce a drawing of the actor Sarah Bernhardt for a poster of the play. Based on a style that he had been developing, he produced a life-sized poster, portraying Bernhardt as a member of Byzantine royalty. This led him to eventually become known as a primary figure in the development of the Art Nouveau form.
Mucha was not an instant success when he started his career, but he kept working on his own style until the right opportunity came along. Success is said to happen only when preparation meets opportunity, and Mucha’s story reminds us that beautiful things can happen when the two finally come together.

다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: Why did Mucha move to Vienna at the age of 19?
How did Mucha support himself while studying in Vienna?
What opportunity gave Mucha his big break in Paris?
How long did Mucha spend creating the poster for Gismonda?
What does Mucha’s story suggest about the relationship between preparation and opportunity?
solution:
Mucha가 크리스마스이브 늦게 혼자 작업하던 중 의뢰를 받았다는 내용만 언급되었을 뿐, 포스터 제작에 실제로 얼마나 시간이 걸렸는지는 언급되지 않았으므로, ④ ‘Mucha는 Gismonda 포스터를 제작하는 데 얼마나 많은 시간을 들였는가?’는 답할 수 없는 질문이다.
오답
① Mucha는 왜 19세의 나이에 비엔나로 이주했는가? (→예술가가 되겠다는 꿈을 이루기 위해 교육을 계속하고자 비엔나로 이주했다.)
② Mucha는 비엔나에서 공부하는 동안 어떻게 자신을 부양했는가? (→잡지에 삽입 광고와 삽화를 그리며 돈을 벌었다.)
③ 어떤 기회가 파리에서 Mucha에게 큰 성공의 계기를 주었는가? (→연극 ‘Gismonda’의 포스터를 그릴 기회를 얻으면서 큰 성공의 계기를 맞았다.)
⑤ Mucha의 이야기는 준비와 기회의 관계에 대해 무엇을 시사하는가? (→성공은 준비가 기회를 만날 때 이루어질 수 있다는 것을 보여 준다.)

body:
Lee Jungseop (1916-1956) is one of the most important artists of 20th century Korean modern art. While White Ox is his most recognized piece, much of his work dealt with the themes of young children and family. Lee used common objects such as animals and children to produce artwork that reminded him of “home.”
This painting, Two Children and Fish and Crab, seems lighthearted at first glance. However, behind this seemingly happy image of children is a sad story. In 1951, Lee and his family took refuge on Jejudo. Although they were fleeing from the war, for Lee, the year that he spent on the island with his wife and children was the highlight of his life. Sadly, it was also the last year of happiness for his family. Poverty from the war led to the separation of his family, as he was forced to send his wife and two sons to Japan for a better chance of survival. During this time of separation, Lee continued to create art, which was his way of ______.
Underneath the cheerful content of the painting is the sadness that Lee felt as he lived alone, far away from his family. But these paintings also allowed him to remember the good times and look forward to a happier future. His ability to express this hope through art brought his work much attention, and his art is a source of comfort to people to this day.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: erasing the painful scars of the war
hiding his deep sorrow from the public
escaping from the harsh reality of poverty
remembering the memories he had with his family
forgetting the pain of being separated from his family

W: Look at that “No Pets Allowed” sign near the entrance of the mall. I think pets should be allowed here.
M: I disagree. I think the “no pets” policy is a good decision.
W: Why do you think so?
M: It keeps the mall safe. Uncontrolled pets can make people uncomfortable and cause trouble.
W: Well, there are many responsible pet owners and well-trained pets.
M: That’s true, but not everyone takes their responsibilities seriously.
W: I think it’s an unfair policy. Pet owners have the right to enjoy the mall with their pets.
M: I get your point, but we have to consider the comfort of all visitors. Some people might have a fear of animals.
W: Hmm... It is challenging to balance the needs of everyone.

다음 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: The woman argues that allowing pets in the mall is justified.
The man believes that permitting animals in the shopping center could lead to potential safety issues and discomfort.
The woman questions whether all pet owners should face restrictions despite the presence of responsible owners and well-trained animals.
The man argues that the comfort of pet owners should take priority over that of other visitors.
The woman eventually acknowledges the difficulty of accommodating the needs of every individual.

body:
[1]
by Emily Mitchell, Editor
In Isaac Asimov’s short story The Fun They Had, a young girl named Margie living in 2155 ⓐreceives her education through a “mechanical teacher.” Her learning takes place one-on-one in her study next to her bedroom. One day, she finds a “real” book on traditional schools from hundreds of years ago and longs to receive a traditional education. She dreams of attending a real school ⓑwhere all the students learn the same things, laugh and play on the playground, and go home together at the end of the day.
[2]
Online education is definitely superior to traditional education. Living in an era ⓒwhen we enjoy technical innovations and boundless connectivity, we should take advantage of what is available in education as well. In the following, I will explore the reasons why online education is a better choice.
First, online education breaks down the barriers of time and space. Learners can access learning programs from anywhere and at any time. For instance, take Khan Academy, an online education program providing free lectures. It started when its founder, Sal Khan, uploaded teaching videos he made for his cousin who was living far away. Now learners from all around the world can enjoy the program’s outstanding lectures on a wide variety of subjects at any time they want.
[3]
“Teaching and learning is the relationship between teachers and students,” Larry Cuban, an education expert from Stanford University, once explained. No matter what advanced technology it is equipped with, it is undeniable that online education focuses mainly on delivering information. It overlooks that education is deeply rooted in the teacher-student relationship, which traditional education is based on. The following will demonstrate the strengths of traditional education in contrast to online education.
First, traditional education has proven more successful in providing an educational environment ⓓin which students can concentrate and learn better. According to a study on students’ level of concentration and understanding in traditional classrooms and online classes, students in traditional classrooms performed better. It seems that ⓔwhat is much easier for students to pay attention and understand the content taught in a traditional classroom because they are learning together.
Traditional education also fosters the development of students’ social and interpersonal skills. Beyond classroom instruction, students interact during their lunch breaks and extracurricular activities. While spending time together and being engaged in various types of interaction, students are exposed to valuable opportunities to learn how to communicate with each other. Consequently, students acquire essential social skills such as collaboration, conflict resolution, and leadership.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⓔ what → it (뒤에 진주어 역할을 하는 to부정사구(to ~ classroom)와 의미상 주어(for students)가 있으므로 이에 상응하는 가주어가 와야 한다. 따라서 what을 it으로 고친다.)

body:
(A)[What / It] is certainly not easy to judge which form of education is better. Online education has advantages such as accessibility, personalized instruction, and innovative teaching materials based on advanced technology. Traditional education, ㉠______ provides a more dynamic learning environment, based on the relationships students and teachers build together.
At present, what seems to be the most effective approach to this debate (B)[is / being] to take advantage of each method by combining them. ㉡______, teachers in a traditional education environment can introduce personalized online programs using AI technology or make use of VR as part of their classroom activities. Combining methods this way can benefit students by making up for (C)[that / what] seems to lack in each method. Selecting the best resources and methods for learners will lead us to the most successful and fulfilling educational outcomes.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

choices: It　being　that
What　is　what
What　being　what
It　is　that
It　is　what
solution:
(A) 뒤에 진주어 역할을 하는 to부정사구(to ~ better)가 있으므로 이에 상응하는 가주어 It이 적절하다.
(B) 관계대명사 what이 이끄는 명사절(what ~ debate)이 주어 역할을 하고 있으며, 그에 이어지는 동사 자리이다. 따라서 what절은 주로 단수 취급하므로, 단수 동사 is가 적절하다.
(C) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(seems ~ method)을 이끌어 making up for의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 관계대명사 what이 적절하다.

by Emily Mitchell, Editor
In Isaac Asimov’s short story The Fun They Had, a young girl named Margie living in 2155 receives her education through a “mechanical teacher.” Her learning takes place one-on-one in her study next to her bedroom. One day, she finds a “real” book on traditional schools from hundreds of years ago and ⓐlongs to receive a traditional education. She dreams of attending a real school where all the students learn the same things, laugh and play on the playground, and go home together at the end of the day.
Margie’s ⓑdesire ⓒreflects the ongoing debate on the merits of online education compared to those of traditional education. As many of us already know, online education is instruction in electronically supported learning environments using multimedia and Internet platforms. Traditional education, on the other hand, generally refers to the ⓓconventional teaching-learning process in a classroom setting in which teachers and students are ⓔpresent together.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞은 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
<보기>
ⓐ long: to want something very much, especially when it seems unlikely to happen soon
ⓑ desire: a strong hope or wish
ⓒ reflect: to show the image of someone or something on the surface of something such as a mirror, water, or glass
ⓓ conventional: traditional and ordinary
ⓔ present: successful, and working in the way that was intended
solution:
ⓐ ~을 간절히 바라다: 특히 곧 일어날 것 같지 않을 때 무언가를 매우 간절히 원하다
ⓑ 바람, 욕구: 강한 희망이나 바람
ⓓ 전통적인, 관습적인: 전통적이고 평범한

Which one do you think is better? We decided to explore this topic by considering the perspectives of our readers. The following represents two sides of the debate.
LETTERS TO THE EDITOR
Innovative Approaches for All Learners
Dear Editor,
Online education is definitely superior to traditional education. ⓐLive in an era in which we enjoy technical innovations and boundless connectivity, we should take advantage of what is available in education as well. In the following, I will explore the reasons ⓑfor which online education is a better choice.
First, online education breaks down the barriers of time and space. Learners can access learning programs from anywhere and at any time. For instance, take Khan Academy, an online education program providing free lectures. It started when its founder, Sal Khan, ⓒuploaded teaching videos he made for his cousin who was living far away. Now learners from all around the world can enjoy the program’s outstanding lectures on a wide variety of subjects at any time they want.
Second, online education caters to (A)______. One of the criticisms of traditional education is that it takes a one-size-fits-all approach that ⓓfail to address the various needs of students. In contrast, online learning can offer a customized learning path for each learner. To achieve this, a computer learning program first assesses each learner’s current level and weaknesses. Based on the assessment, each learner is offered personalized online lessons and more detailed explanations when necessary. This kind of personalized feedback process can be highly interactive and motivate learners to reach higher levels of achievement.
Finally, online education uses advanced technology such as multimedia materials or virtual simulations to provide more engaging and impactful learning experiences. For example, students can learn history more effectively by using virtual reality programs, ⓔwhich can show them realistic details of famous historical sites or allow them to travel back in time.

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: uniform learning methods that treat all students equally
constant teacher supervision that corrects students' mistakes immediately
unlimited access to free educational resources for independent learners
personalized learning opportunities that meet the various needs of each learner
standardized assessments that rank learners according to fixed academic criteria
solution: 정답은 ④ 이다. (해설 없음)

body:
Dear Editor,
“Teaching and learning is the relationship between teachers and students,” Larry Cuban, an education expert from Stanford University, once explained. No matter what advanced technology it is equipped with, it is undeniable that online education focuses mainly on delivering information. It overlooks that education is deeply rooted in the teacher-student relationship, which traditional education is based on. The following will demonstrate the strengths of traditional education in contrast to online education.
First, traditional education has proven more successful in providing an educational environment where students can concentrate and learn better. According to a study on students’ level of concentration and understanding in traditional classrooms and online classes, students in traditional classrooms performed better. It seems that it is much easier for students to pay attention and understand the content taught in a traditional classroom because they are learning together.
Traditional education also fosters the development of students’ social and interpersonal skills. Beyond classroom instruction, students interact during their lunch breaks and extracurricular activities. ⓐ함께 시간을 보내고 다양한 유형의 상호 작용에 참여하는 동안, 학생들은 서로 소통하는 방법을 배울 수 있는 귀중한 기회에 노출됩니다. Consequently, students acquire essential social skills such as collaboration, conflict resolution, and leadership.

How was the study on students’ levels of concentration and understanding in traditional classrooms and online classes conducted?

What specific social skills do students acquire through traditional education?

Grandma Moses
When it seems too late
At the Well. This painting, with its warm colors and detailed portrayal of an ordinary day on a farm, fills the viewer with a sense of calm. In this depiction of another peaceful day, we see farmers go about their day — sweeping, pushing a cart, and drawing water out of the well. We can also see cows and goats grazing on the grass, alongside the farmers. This painting was done by Anna Mary Robertson Moses (1860-1961), better known as Grandma Moses, one of the most well-known figures in the world of Naive art.
Before she started painting, Grandma Moses lived on a farm, ⓐsold homemade foods at local markets while raising her five children. She started painting in her 70s but had become an internationally recognized artist by the time she passed away at the age of 101. During that time, she produced more than 1,600 paintings. These paintings portray a simple lifestyle in the rural countryside, bringing about a sense of nostalgia about the past.
Her first paintings were done with leftover crayons and old paintbrushes that had been used by her grandchildren.
(A) Then, one day in 1939, an art collector ⓑnaming Louis Calder noticed her paintings in the window of a drugstore. Realizing the beauty of her work, he organized exhibitions of her drawings, which ⓒwas all a big hit with the public, and the rest is history.
(B) She started by making these paintings to give away as gifts. Later, she tried selling them at local markets, but they received little or no attention.
(C) The exhibitions brought the work of Grandma Moses to the public, ⓓallowed people from all walks of life to appreciate the calming beauty of her everyday life.
The story of Grandma Moses is a reminder that it is never too late ⓔaccomplish our dreams.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 정답은 ② 이다. (해설 없음)

Many works of art bring us happiness or comfort by their existence alone. Take, for example, the work of Arthur Elsley. His paintings of children and their pets have made people smile for over a century. The work of another artist, Mark Rothko, might be more recognizable. The solid colors in his paintings bring to mind the diversity of human emotions, helping those who view them feel a sense of warmth and comfort.
Artwork, however, is more deeply appreciated with a deeper understanding of the artist and the experiences that helped produce it. body:
Lee Jungseop
Lee Jungseop (1916-1956) is one of the most important artists of 20th century Korean modern art. While White Ox is his most recognized piece, much of his work dealt with the themes of young children and family. Lee used common objects such as animals and children to produce artwork that reminded him of “home.”
This painting, Two Children and Fish and Crab, seems lighthearted at first glance. However, behind this seemingly happy image of children is a sad story. In 1951, Lee and his family took refuge on Jejudo. Although they were fleeing from the war, for Lee, the year that he spent on the island with his wife and children was the highlight of his life. Sadly, it was also the last year of happiness for his family. Poverty from the war led to the separation of his family, as he was forced (A)[sending / to send] his wife and two sons to Japan for a better chance of survival. During this time of separation, Lee continued to create art, which was his way of remembering the memories (B)[which / what] he had with his family.
Underneath the cheerful content of the painting is the sadness (C)[what / that] Lee felt as he lived alone, far away from his family. But these paintings also allowed him to remember the good times and look forward to a happier future. His ability to express this hope through art brought his work much attention, and his art is a source of comfort to people to this day.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: sending / which / that
to send / which / that
sending / what / that
to send / which / what
to send / what / what
solution:
(A) 동사 force의 5형식 구문 ‘force+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)’이 ‘be forced+to부정사‘의 수동태 구문으로 쓰이므로 was forced 뒤에 to부정사 to send가 적절하다.
(B) 동사의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(he ~ family)을 이끌어 명사구 the memories를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 목적격 관계대명사 which가 적절하다.
*(B)는 원래 지문에서 생략되었음
(C) 동사의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(Lee felt)을 이끌어 명사구 the sadness를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 목적격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다.

Before she started painting, Grandma Moses lived on a farm, selling homemade foods at local markets while raising her five children. She started painting in her 70s but had become an internationally recognized artist by the time she passed away at the age of 101. During that time, she produced more than 1,600 paintings. These paintings portray a simple lifestyle in the rural countryside, bringing about a sense of nostalgia about the past.
Her first paintings were done with leftover crayons and old paintbrushes that had been used by her grandchildren. She started by making these paintings to give away as gifts. Later, she tried selling them at local markets, but they received little or no attention. Then, one day in 1939, an art collector named Louis Calder noticed her paintings in the window of a drugstore. Realizing the beauty of her work, he organized exhibitions of her drawings, which were all a big hit with the public, and the rest is history. The exhibitions brought the work of Grandma Moses to the public, allowing people from all walks of life to appreciate the calming beauty of her everyday life. The story of Grandma Moses is a reminder that it is never too late to accomplish our dreams.

body:
Grandma Moses
At the Well. This painting, with its warm colors and detailed portrayal of an ordinary day on a farm, fills the viewer with a sense of calm. In this depiction of another peaceful day, we see farmers go about their day — sweeping, pushing a cart, and drawing water out of the well. We can also see cows and goats grazing on the grass, alongside the farmers. This painting was done by Anna Mary Robertson Moses (1860-1961), better known as Grandma Moses, one of the most well-known figures in the world of Naive art.
Before she started painting, Grandma Moses lived on a farm, selling homemade foods at local markets while raising her five children. She started painting in her 70s but had become an internationally recognized artist by the time she passed away at the age of 101. During that time, she produced more than 1,600 paintings. These paintings portray a simple lifestyle in the rural countryside, bringing about a sense of nostalgia about the past.
Her first paintings were done with leftover crayons and old paintbrushes that had been used by her grandchildren. She started by making these paintings to give away as gifts. Later, she tried selling them at local markets, but they received (A)______. Then, one day in 1939, an art collector named Louis Calder noticed her paintings in the window of a drugstore. Realizing the beauty of her work, he organized exhibitions of her drawings, which were (B)______ with the public, and the rest is history. The exhibitions brought the work of Grandma Moses to the public, allowing people from all walks of life to appreciate the calming beauty of her everyday life. The story of Grandma Moses is a reminder that it is never too late to accomplish our dreams.

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B)
choices: little or no attention / complete failures
hardly any notice / complete failures
little or no attention / wildly successful
widespread acclaim / public triumphs

solution:
(A) 앞 절에서 Grandma Moses가 지역 시장에서 자신의 그림들을 판매하려고 시도했다고 했고, 빈칸이 있는 절은 상반된 내용을 나타내는 but으로 연결되어 있으므로, 그림들이 판매에 성공하지 못했다는 흐름이 이어져야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ‘거의 또는 전혀 관심을 받지 못한’, ‘거의 어떠한 주목도 받지 못한’이 적절하다.

body:
Grandma Moses
At the Well. This painting, with its warm colors and detailed portrayal of an ordinary day on a farm, fills the viewer with a sense of calm. In this depiction of another peaceful day, we see farmers go about their day — sweeping, pushing a cart, and drawing water out of the well. We can also see cows and goats grazing on the grass, alongside the farmers. This painting was done by Anna Mary Robertson Moses (1860-1961), better known as Grandma Moses, one of the most well-known figures in the world of Naive art.
Before she started painting, Grandma Moses lived on a farm, selling homemade foods at local markets while raising her five children. She started painting in her 70s but had become an internationally recognized artist by the time she passed away at the age of 101. During that time, she produced more than 1,600 paintings. These paintings portray a simple lifestyle in the rural countryside, bringing about a sense of nostalgia about the past.
Her first paintings were done with leftover crayons and old paintbrushes that had been used by her grandchildren. She started by making these paintings to give away as gifts. Later, she tried selling them at local markets, but they received (A)______. Then, one day in 1939, an art collector named Louis Calder noticed her paintings in the window of a drugstore. Realizing the beauty of her work, he organized exhibitions of her drawings, which were (B)______ with the public, and the rest is history. The exhibitions brought the work of Grandma Moses to the public, allowing people from all walks of life to appreciate the calming beauty of her everyday life. The story of Grandma Moses is a reminder that it is never too late to accomplish our dreams.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 모두 고르면?
choices: The painting At the Well by Grandma Moses depicts a quiet farm day, showing farmers at work alongside grazing animals.
Before Grandma Moses took up painting, she used to sell homemade foods at local markets.
Grandma Moses started her painting career when she was young and went on to create more than 1,600 works during her life.
Grandma Moses’s first paintings were created for sale at local markets.
The exhibitions arranged by Louis Calder introduced the calm beauty of Grandma Moses’s paintings to a wider audience.
solution:
Grandma Moses는 70대에 그림을 그리기 시작해, 101세의 나이로 세상을 떠나기 전까지 1,600점 이상의 그림을 그렸다고 했으므로 ③ ‘Grandma Moses는 젊었을 때 그림 경력을 시작했고, 평생 동안 1,600점이 넘는 작품을 계속해서 만들어 냈다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
Grandma Moses의 초창기 그림들은 선물로 나눠주기 위해 그림들을 그렸다고 했으므로 ④ ’Grandma Moses의 첫 번째 그림들은 지역 시장에서 판매하기 위해 만들어졌다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① Grandma Moses의 ‘At the Well’이라는 그림은 조용한 농장의 하루를 묘사하며, 일하는 농부들과 풀을 뜯는 동물들을 보여 준다.
② Grandma Moses가 그림을 그리기 시작하기 전에, 그녀는 지역 시장에서 직접 만든 음식들을 팔곤 했다.
take ~ up ~을 시작하다
⑤ Louis Calder가 마련한 전시회는 Grandma Moses의 그림의 차분한 아름다움을 더 많은 사람들에게 알렸다.

body:
Lee Jungseop
Lee Jungseop (1916-1956) is one of the most important artists of 20th century Korean modern art. While White Ox is his most recognized piece, much of his work dealt with the themes of young children and family. Lee used common objects such as animals and children to produce artwork that reminded him of “home.”
This painting, Two Children and Fish and Crab, seems lighthearted at first glance. However, behind this seemingly happy image of children is a sad story. In 1951, Lee and his family took refuge on Jejudo. Although they were fleeing from the war, for Lee, the year that he spent on the island with his wife and children was the highlight of his life. Sadly, it was also the last year of happiness for his family. Poverty from the war led to the separation of his family, as he was forced to send his wife and two sons to Japan for a better chance of survival. During this time of separation, Lee continued to create art, which was his way of remembering the memories he had with his family.
Underneath the cheerful content of the painting is the sadness that Lee felt as he lived alone, far away from his family. But these paintings also allowed him to remember the good times and look forward to a happier future. His ability to express this hope through art brought his work much attention, and his art is a source of comfort to people to this day.

by Emily Mitchell, Editor
In Isaac Asimov’s short story The Fun They Had, a young girl named Margie (A)[lives / living] in 2155 receives her education through a “mechanical teacher.” Her learning takes place one-on-one in her study next to her bedroom. One day, she finds a “real” book on traditional schools from hundreds of years ago and longs to receive a traditional education. She dreams of attending a real school (B)[where / which] all the students learn the same things, laugh and play on the playground, and go home together at the end of the day.
Margie’s desire reflects the ongoing debate on the merits of online education compared to (C)[that / those] of traditional education. As many of us already know, online education is instruction in electronically supported learning environments using multimedia and Internet platforms. Traditional education, on the other hand, generally refers to the conventional teaching-learning process in a classroom setting in which teachers and students are present together.
Which one do you think is better? We decided to explore this topic by considering the perspectives of our readers. The following represents two sides of the debate.

choices: lives / where / those
living / where / that
lives / which / that
living / where / those
living / which / those
solution:
(A) 뒤에 문장의 동사 receives가 있으므로, 분사구 named Margie에 이어 명사구 a young girl을 수식하는 분사 자리이다. 따라서 수식받는 명사구 a young girl이 2155년에 ‘사는’ 주체이자 live는 자동사이므로, 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 living이 적절하다.
(B) 완전한 절(all ~ day)을 이끌어 장소를 나타내는 선행사 a real school을 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 관계부사 where가 적절하다.
(C) 온라인 교육의 장점들(the merits of online education)과 전통적 교육(traditional education)의 장점들을 비교하고 있으므로 ‘장점들’을 뜻하는 복수명사구 the merits를 대신하는 복수대명사 those가 적절하다.

body:
LETTERS TO THE EDITOR
Innovative Approaches for All Learners
Dear Editor,
Online education is definitely superior to traditional education. ㉠Living in an era which we enjoy technical innovations and boundless connectivity, we should take advantage of what is available in education as well. In the following, I will explore the reasons why online education is a better choice.
First, online education breaks down the barriers of time and space. Learners can access learning programs from anywhere and at any time. For instance, take Khan Academy, an online education program providing free lectures. It started when its founder, Sal Khan, uploaded teaching videos he made for his cousin who was living far away. Now learners from all around the world can enjoy the program’s outstanding lectures on a wide variety of subjects at any time they want.
Second, online education caters to personalized learning opportunities that meet the various needs of each learner. (A) One of the criticisms of traditional education is that it takes a one-size-fits-all approach that fails to address the various needs of students. (B) In contrast, online learning can offer a customized learning path for each learner. (C) Based on the assessment, each learner is offered personalized online lessons and more detailed explanations when necessary. (D) This kind of personalized feedback process can be highly interactive and motivate learners to reach higher levels of achievement. (E)
Finally, online education uses advanced technology such as multimedia materials or virtual simulations to provide more engaging and impactful learning experiences. For example, students can learn history more effectively by using virtual reality programs, ㉡which can show them realistic details of famous historical sites or allow them traveling back in time.
Advances in technology can make education so much better. Learning anywhere and at any time and receiving personalized lessons can make learning more effective and rewarding. It is evident that the future of education lies in online education.
Best regards,
Ethan Williams
윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
To achieve this, a computer learning program first assesses each learner’s current level and weaknesses.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘이를 달성하기 위해, 컴퓨터 학습 프로그램이 각 학습자의 현재 수준과 약점을 먼저 평가합니다.’라는 의미이다. 여기서 this는 앞에서 제시된 목표를 가리키므로, 주어진 문장은 온라인 학습이 각 학습자에게 맞춤형 학습 경로를 제공할 수 있다는 내용 뒤에 위치해야 한다. 또한 본문의 the assessment(그 평가)는 주어진 문장의 assesses(평가하다)에서 언급된 평가를 가리키므로, 주어진 문장은 the assessment가 등장하는 문장보다 앞에 위치해야 한다. 따라서 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은 (C)이다.

body:
“Teaching and learning is the relationship between teachers and students,” Larry Cuban, an education expert from Stanford University, once explained. No matter what advanced technology it is equipped with, it is undeniable ⓐwhat online education focuses mainly on delivering information. It overlooks ⓑthat education is deeply rooted in the teacher-student relationship, which traditional education is based on. The following will demonstrate the strengths of traditional education in contrast to online education.
First, traditional education has proven ⓒmore successful in providing an educational environment where students can concentrate and learn better. According to a study on students’ level of concentration and understanding in traditional classrooms and online classes, students in traditional classrooms performed better. ㉠함께 학습하고 있기 때문에, 학생들이 주의를 기울이고 전통적 교실에서 배우는 내용을 이해하는 것이 훨씬 더 쉬운 것으로 보입니다.
Traditional education also fosters the development of students’ social and interpersonal skills. Beyond classroom instruction, students interact during their lunch breaks and extracurricular activities. While spending time together and being engaged in various types of interaction, students are exposed to valuable opportunities to learn how ⓓto communicate with each other. Consequently, students acquire essential social skills such as collaboration, conflict resolution, and leadership.
Finally, traditional education offers hands-on and practical learning opportunities. Subjects such as lab sciences and vocational training rely heavily on experiments and direct guidance from instructors. For instance, in a biology class, students learn how to handle a microscope, and ⓔobserve the shape of a cell through a microscope for the first time will present them with a truly engaging experience. Online platforms may provide simulations and virtual tools, but they cannot fully substitute the hands-on experiences offered by traditional classrooms.
In short, effective learning requires meaningful relationships between teachers and students, as well as among peers. This interpersonal connection represents the main advantage of traditional education. ⓕGuided by strong relationships, students can concentrate better, acquire interpersonal skills, and enjoy hands-on learning experiences. Traditional education makes all of this ⓖpossibly.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어색한 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓐ what → that (완전한 절(online ~ information)을 이끌어 가주어 it에 상응하는 진주어절을 이루어야 하므로 what을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다.)
ⓔ observe → observing (뒤에 동사 will이 있으므로, 뒤의 the shape ~ time을 이끌어 주어부를 이룰 수 있는 동명사가 와야 한다. 따라서 동사원형 observe를 동명사 observing으로 고친다.)
ⓖ possibly → possible (‘…를 ~하게 만들다’의 의미를 갖는 5형식 동사 make는 ‘make+목적어+목적격보어’의 구조로 쓰이며, 목적격보어 자리에 부사는 올 수 없다. 따라서 makes의 목적어 all of this 뒤에 위치한 목적격보어가 되도록 부사 possibly를 형용사 possible로 고친다.)
오답

It is certainly not easy to judge which form of education is better. Online education has advantages such as accessibility, personalized instruction, and innovative teaching materials based on advanced technology. Traditional education, on the other hand, provides a more dynamic learning environment, based on the relationships students and teachers build together.
At present, what seems to be the most effective approach to this debate is to take advantage of each method by combining them. For example, teachers in a traditional education environment can introduce personalized online programs using AI technology or make use of VR as part of their classroom activities. Combining methods this way can benefit students by making up for what seems to lack in each method. Selecting the best resources and methods for learners will lead us to the most successful and fulfilling educational outcomes.

Many works of art ⓐbring us happiness or comfort by their existence alone. Take, for example, the work of Arthur Elsley. His paintings of children and their pets have made people ⓑto smile for over a century. The work of another artist, Mark Rothko, might be more recognizable. The solid colors in his paintings bring to mind the diversity of human emotions, helping those ⓒwho view them feel a sense of warmth and comfort.
Artwork, however, is more deeply appreciated with a deeper understanding of the artist and the experiences ⓓwhat helped produce it. We are going to explore the lives of three artists whose art has inspired people from different cultures and generations. As their life experiences became the inspiration for their art, understanding the stories behind their work will not only help us better ⓔappreciate their work but also inspire us.
윗글의 내용과 (A)~(E)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?
(A) Arthur Elsley’s paintings have delighted viewers by depicting children with their pets. (T/F)
(B) Mark Rothko’s use of color makes viewers think about the wide variety of human emotions. (T/F)
(C) Mark Rothko’s artwork might be less recognizable to the public compared to the works of Arthur Elsley. (T/F)
(D) Learning about an artist’s life story prevents us from appreciating the artwork deeply. (T/F)
(E) The life experiences of the three artists to be explored served as inspiration for their artwork. (T/F)
choices: F-T-F-T-F
T-T-F-F-F
T-T-T-F-T
T-T-F-F-T
T-T-F-T-T
solution:
차례대로 T-T-F-F-T이다.
(A) Arthur Elsley의 그림들은 아이들과 그들의 반려동물들을 묘사함으로써 감상자들을 기쁘게 해 왔다. (일치)

(C) Mark Rothko의 작품은 Arthur Elsley의 작품과 비교하면 대중에게 덜(→더 잘) 알아볼 수 있을지도 모른다. (불일치)

(E) 앞으로 살펴볼 세 예술가의 삶의 경험은 그들의 작품에 대한 영감으로서의 역할을 한다. (일치)

body:
Grandma Moses
At the Well. This painting, with its warm colors and detailed portrayal of an ordinary day on a farm, fills the viewer with a sense of calm. In this depiction of another peaceful day, we see farmers go about their day — sweeping, pushing a cart, and drawing water out of the well. We can also see cows and goats grazing on the grass, alongside the farmers. This painting was done by Anna Mary Robertson Moses (1860-1961), better known as Grandma Moses, one of the most well-known figures in the world of Naive art.
Before she started painting, Grandma Moses lived on a farm, selling homemade foods at local markets while raising her five children. She started painting in her 70s but had become an internationally recognized artist by the time she passed away at the age of 101. During that time, she produced more than 1,600 paintings. These paintings portray a simple lifestyle in the rural countryside, bringing about a sense of nostalgia about the past.
Her first paintings were done with leftover crayons and old paintbrushes that had been used by her grandchildren. She started by making these paintings to give away as gifts. Later, she tried selling them at local markets, but they received little or no attention. Then, one day in 1939, an art collector named Louis Calder noticed her paintings in the window of a drugstore. (A)그녀의 작품의 아름다움을 깨닫고 그는 그녀의 그림 전시회들을 열었는데, 이는 모두 대중에게 큰 인기를 끌었고, 그 후의 일은 다들 아는 대로이다. The exhibitions brought the work of Grandma Moses to the public, allowing people from all walks of life to appreciate the calming beauty of her everyday life. The story of Grandma Moses is a reminder that it is never too late to accomplish our dreams.
윗글을 다음과 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
Grandma Moses turned memories of simple rural life into (A)______ paintings and, despite beginning her artistic career late and receiving little attention at first, eventually gained worldwide recognition with the help of an art collector, showing that age is not a (B)______ to pursuing one’s dreams.
(A) (B)
choices: soothing support
disturbing obstacle
comforting barrier
unsettling benefit
calming aid
solution:
요약문 Grandma Moses는 소박한 농촌 생활의 기억을 (A)위안을 주는 그림으로 표현했고, 늦은 나이에 화가의 길을 시작해 처음에는 거의 주목받지 못했음에도 미술 수집가의 도움으로 결국 전 세계적인 인정을 받으면서, 나이가 자신의 꿈을 추구하는 데 (B)장벽이 되지 않는다는 것을 보여 주었다.

① 마음을 편안하게 하는 지원
② 마음을 불편하게 하는 장애물
④ 마음을 편치 않게 하는 이점
⑤ 마음을 차분하게 하는 도움

Lee Jungseop
Hope within life difficulties
Lee Jungseop (1916-1956) is one of the most important artists of 20th century Korean modern art. While White Ox is his most recognized piece, much of his work dealt with the themes of young children and family. Lee used common objects such as animals and children to produce artwork that reminded him of “home.”
This painting, Two Children and Fish and Crab, seems (A)lighthearted at first glance. However, behind this seemingly happy image of children is a sad story. In 1951, Lee and his family took refuge on Jejudo. Although they were fleeing from the war, for Lee, the year that he spent on the island with his wife and children ⓐwere the highlight of his life. Sadly, it was also the last year of (B)happiness for his family. Poverty from the war led to the (C)reunion of his family, as he was ⓑforced to send his wife and two sons to Japan for a better chance of survival. During this time of separation, Lee continued to create art, ⓒwhich was his way of remembering the memories he had with his family.
Underneath the cheerful content of the painting ⓓis the sadness that Lee felt as he lived alone, far away from his family. But these paintings also (D)allowed him to remember the good times and look forward to a happier future. His ability ⓔto express this hope through art brought his work much attention, and his art is a source of (E)comfort to people to this day.
윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: (C) reunion(재회) → separation(헤어짐)

body:
Alfonse Mucha (1860-1939) was one of the first Art Nouveau artists, which led to this form of art being referred to as the “Mucha Style.” His style became famous later on in his life and is used often, even to this day. His fame, however, did not happen overnight.
As a younger artist, Mucha was rejected when he applied for his local art school, but he did not give up. Holding on to his dream of one day becoming an artist, he moved to Vienna at the age of 19 to continue his education. After working different jobs to support himself during his studies, he finally finished his schooling and 7 years later, moved to Paris.
In Paris, Mucha made money drawing inserts and illustrations for magazines but also (A)[ceased / continued] working on his own art. His big break came much later in 1894, when he (B)[missed / landed] the opportunity to draw a poster for the play Gismonda. He was working alone late on Christmas Eve when he was commissioned to produce a drawing of the actor Sarah Bernhardt for a poster of the play. Based on a style that he had been developing, he produced a life-sized poster, portraying Bernhardt as a member of Byzantine royalty. This led him to eventually become known as a primary figure in the development of the Art Nouveau form.
Mucha was not an instant success when he started his career, but he kept working on his own style until the right opportunity came along. Success is said to happen only when preparation meets opportunity, and Mucha’s story reminds us that beautiful things can happen when the two finally (C)[move apart / come together].
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: ceased landed come together
continued missed come together
continued landed come together
ceased missed move apart
continued landed move apart
solution:
(A) 마지막 단락에서 Mucha는 처음부터 성공을 거두지는 못했지만, 기회가 생길 때까지 자신만의 양식을 계속해 나갔다고 했으므로 삽입 광고와 삽화를 그려 돈을 벌면서 자신의 예술 작업도 계속했다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 continued(~을 계속했다)가 적절하다.
cease ~을 중단하다
(B) Mucha는 이때 연극 ‘Gismonda’의 포스터를 그릴 기회를 잡아 마침내 아르누보 양식 발전의 주요 인물로 알려지게 된 것이므로, landed(~을 얻었다, 잡았다)가 적절하다.
miss ~을 놓치다
(C) Mucha는 적절한 기회가 생길 때까지 자신만의 양식을 계속해 나갔고 성공은 준비가 기회와 만날 때만 이루어진다고 언급하고 있으므로, 그 두 가지가 마침내 결합할 때 아름다운 일들이 일어날 수 있다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 come together(결합하다)가 적절하다.
move apart 서로 멀어지다

When and how did Grandma Moses start her career as a painter?
How many works did Grandma Moses create before she passed away?
Why did Grandma Moses’s paintings receive little or no attention at first?
How were Grandma Moses’s paintings brought to the public?
solution:
지역 시장에서 판매를 시도했으나 관심을 끌지 못했다고 언급될 뿐, 관심을 받지 못한 구체적인 이유는 알 수 없으므로 ④ ‘Grandma Moses의 그림은 왜 처음에는 거의 또는 전혀 관심을 받지 못했는가?’는 답할 수 없는 질문이다.

② Grandma Moses는 언제 그리고 어떻게 화가로서의 경력을 시작했는가? (→70대에 그림을 그리기 시작했으며, 손주들이 사용했던 남은 크레용과 오래된 붓을 이용했다.)
③ Grandma Moses는 세상을 떠나기 전까지 얼마나 많은 그림을 그렸는가? (→그녀는 1,600점 이상의 그림을 그렸다.)
⑤ Grandma Moses의 그림들은 어떻게 대중에게 알려지게 되었는가? (→미술 수집가 Louis Calder가 그녀의 그림을 발견한 뒤 전시회를 열면서 대중에게 알려지게 되었다.)

body:
In Paris, Mucha made money drawing inserts and illustrations for magazines but also continued working on his own art. His big break came much later in 1894, when he landed the opportunity to draw a poster for the play Gismonda. He was working alone late on Christmas Eve when he was commissioned to produce a drawing of the actor Sarah Bernhardt for a poster of the play. Based on a style that he had been developing, he produced a life-sized poster, (A)[portrayed / portraying] Bernhardt as a member of Byzantine royalty. This led him to eventually (B)[become / becoming] known as a primary figure in the development of the Art Nouveau form.
Mucha was not an instant success when he started his career, but he kept working on his own style until the right opportunity came along. Success is said to happen only when preparation meets opportunity, and Mucha’s story reminds us (C)[what / that] beautiful things can happen when the two finally come together.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: portrayed become that
portraying become that
portrayed becoming that
portraying become what
portraying becoming what
solution:
(A) 콤마(,) 앞의 완전한 절(he produced ~ poster)에 접속사 없이 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 he가 ‘묘사하는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 portraying이 적절하다.
(B) 동사 led는 ‘lead+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)(~가 …하도록 이끌다)의 5형식 구문으로 쓰이므로 목적격보어로 to부정사구가 와야 한다. 따라서 부사가 to부정사 사이에 위치한 분리부정사의 형태 ’to+부사+동사원형’로 to eventually 뒤에 동사원형 become이 오는 것이 적절하다.
(C) 완전한 절(beautiful things ~ together)을 이끌어 4형식 동사 reminds의 직접목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 명사절 접속사 that이 적절하다.

body:
Lee Jungseop
Lee Jungseop (1916-1956) is one of the most important artists of 20th century Korean modern art. While White Ox is his most recognized piece, much of his work dealt with the themes of young children and family. Lee used common objects such as animals and children to produce artwork that reminded him of “home.”
This painting, Two Children and Fish and Crab, seems lighthearted at first glance. (A) In 1951, Lee and his family took refuge on Jejudo. (B) Although they were fleeing from the war, for Lee, the year that he spent on the island with his wife and children was the highlight of his life. (C) Sadly, it was also the last year of happiness for his family. (D) Poverty from the war led to the separation of his family, as he was forced to send his wife and two sons to Japan for a better chance of survival. (E) During this time of separation, Lee continued to create art, which was his way of remembering the memories he had with his family.
Underneath the cheerful content of the painting is the sadness that Lee felt as he lived alone, far away from his family. But these paintings also allowed him to remember the good times and look forward to a happier future. His ability ⓐ______ brought his work much attention, and his art is a source of comfort to people to this day.
윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
However, behind this seemingly happy image of children is a sad story.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘그러나 겉보기에는 행복해 보이는 이 아이들의 모습 뒤에는 슬픈 이야기가 있다.’라는 뜻이며, 역접을 나타내는 연결사 However가 쓰였으므로 이 문장 앞에는 겉보기에는 행복해 보이는 대상에 대한 내용이 와야 하며, 이 문장 뒤에는 슬픈 이야기(a sad story)에 대한 설명이 이어져야 한다. 따라서 ‘두 아이와 물고기와 게’라는 그림이 언뜻 보기에 쾌활해 보인다는 문장 뒤이자 이중섭과 그의 가족이 제주도로 피난을 갔다는 문장 앞인 (A)에 들어가야 한다.

body:
Grandma Moses
When it seems too late
At the Well. This painting, with its warm colors and detailed portrayal of an ordinary day on a farm, fills the viewer with a sense of calm. In this depiction of another peaceful day, we see farmers go about their day ─sweeping, pushing a cart, and drawing water out of the well. We can also see cows and goats grazing on the grass, alongside the farmers. This painting was done by Anna Mary Robertson Moses (1860-1961), better known as Grandma Moses, one of the most well-known figures in the world of Naive art.
Before she started painting, Grandma Moses lived on a farm, selling homemade foods at local markets while raising her five children. She started painting in her 70s but had become an internationally recognized artist by the time she passed away at the age of 101. During that time, she produced more than 1,600 paintings. These paintings portray a simple lifestyle in the rural countryside, bringing about a sense of nostalgia about the past.
Her first paintings were done with leftover crayons and old paintbrushes that had been used by her grandchildren. She started by making these paintings to give away as gifts. Later, she tried selling them at local markets, but they received little or no attention. Then, one day in 1939, an art collector named Louis Calder noticed her paintings in the window of a drugstore. Realizing the beauty of her work, he organized exhibitions of her drawings, which were all a big hit with the public, and the rest is history. The exhibitions brought the work of Grandma Moses to the public, allowing people from all walks of life to appreciate the calming beauty of her everyday life. The story of Grandma Moses is a reminder that (A)______.
윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: artistic recognition depends on starting one’s career at a young age
personal hardship motivate artists to achieve meaningful success
our early experiences determine the kind of art we will create
success comes only after years of professional training
it is never too late to accomplish our dreams
solution:
두 번째 단락에서 Grandma Moses는 70대에 그림을 시작했지만 국제적으로 인정받는 예술가가 되었고, 101세까지 1,600점이 넘는 작품을 남겼다고 설명했으므로 이야기가 우리에게 늦은 나이여도 여전히 꿈을 이룰 수 있다는 것을 상기시켜 준다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ⑤ ‘우리의 꿈을 이루기에 결코 너무 늦은 때는 없다’가 적절하다.
오답
① 예술적 인정을 받는 것은 젊은 나이에 경력을 시작하는 것에 달려 있다
② 개인적인 고난은 예술가들이 의미 있는 성공을 이루도록 동기를 부여할 수 있다
③ 우리의 어린 시절 경험이 우리가 어떤 종류의 예술을 창작하게 될지를 결정한다
④ 성공은 오직 수년간의 전문적인 훈련 후에 찾아온다

body:
by Emily Mitchell, Editor
In Isaac Asimov’s short story The Fun They Had, a young girl ⓐnamed Margie living in 2155 receives her education through a “mechanical teacher.” Her learning takes place one-on-one in her study next to her bedroom. One day, she finds a “real” book on traditional schools from hundreds of years ago and longs ⓑto receive a traditional education. She dreams of attending a real school where all the students learn the same things, laugh and play on the playground, and go home together at the end of the day.
Margie’s desire reflects the ongoing debate on the merits of online education compared to those of traditional education. As many of us already know, online education is instruction in electronically supported learning environments ⓒusing multimedia and Internet platforms. Traditional education, on the other hand, generally refers to the conventional teaching-learning process in a classroom setting ⓓwhich teachers and students are present together.
Which one do you think ⓔis better? We decided to explore this topic by considering the perspectives of our readers. The following represents two sides of the debate.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓓ which → where 또는 in which (완전한 절(teachers ~ together)을 이끌어 a classroom setting을 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 관계부사 또는 ‘전치사+관계대명사’ 형태로 써야 한다. 따라서 which를 관계부사 where로 고치거나, 전치사 in을 함께 쓴 in which로 고친다.)
*본문에는 in which가 쓰였음
오답
ⓐ 뒤에 문장의 동사 receives가 있으므로, 명사구 a young girl을 수식하는 분사 자리이며, a young girl이 Margie라고 ‘이름 지어진’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 named는 적절하다.
ⓑ 동사 long은 to부정사를 목적어로 취해 ‘~하기를 간절히 바라다’라는 뜻으로 쓰이므로 longs의 목적어 자리의 to receive는 적절하다.
ⓒ 명사구 electronically supported learning environments를 수식하는 분사 자리로, 수식받는 명사구가 ‘사용하는’ 주체이며 뒤에 목적어 multimedia and Internet platforms가 이어지므로, 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 using은 적절하다.
ⓔ think, suppose, believe 등이 주절의 동사일 때 의문사가 있는 의문문이 뒤에 이어지면 의문사가 맨 앞으로 이동하므로, ‘do you think+which is better’에서 which가 앞으로 이동하고 남은 is better가 think 바로 뒤에 이어져야 한다. 따라서 think 뒤에 이어지는 is는 알맞다.

by Emily Mitchell, Editor
In Isaac Asimov’s short story The Fun They Had, a young girl ⓐnamed Margie living in 2155 receives her education through a “mechanical teacher.” Her learning takes place one-on-one in her study next to her bedroom. One day, she finds a “real” book on traditional schools from hundreds of years ago and longs ⓑto receive a traditional education. She dreams of attending a real school where all the students learn the same things, laugh and play on the playground, and go home together at the end of the day.
Margie’s desire reflects the ongoing debate on the merits of online education compared to those of traditional education. As many of us already know, online education is instruction in electronically supported learning environments ⓒusing multimedia and Internet platforms. Traditional education, on the other hand, generally refers to the conventional teaching-learning process in a classroom setting ⓓwhich teachers and students are present together.
Which one do you think ⓔis better? We decided to explore this topic by considering the perspectives of our readers. The following represents two sides of the debate.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: In the story The Fun They Had, a “mechanical teacher” provides Margie with individual lessons in her home.
In the school Margie dreams of, classmates share lessons, enjoy recreation, and leave for home together.
The story The Fun They Had is related to the debate over online versus traditional education.
Various forms of media and Internet platforms form the basis of online instruction.
Traditional education keeps teachers and learners in separate physical spaces.
solution:
전통적 교육은 일반적으로 교사와 학생이 함께 있는 교실 환경에서의 전통적인 교수-학습 과정을 의미한다고 언급되었으므로, ⑤ ‘전통적 교육은 교사와 학습자를 서로 분리된 물리적 공간에 있게 한다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① ‘The Fun They Had’라는 이야기에서, ‘기계 선생님’이 집에서 Margie에게 개별 수업을 제공한다.
② Margie가 꿈꾸는 학교에서는, 반 친구들이 함께 수업을 받고, 여가 활동을 즐기며, 함께 집으로 간다.
③ ‘The Fun They Had’라는 이야기는 온라인 교육과 전통 교육을 둘러싼 논쟁과 관련이 있다.
④ 다양한 형태의 미디어와 인터넷 플랫폼이 온라인 수업의 기반을 형성한다.

LETTERS TO THE EDITOR
Innovative Approaches for All Learners
Dear Editor,
Online education is definitely superior to traditional education. ⓐ우리는 기술적 혁신과 무한한 연결성을 누리는 시대에서 살아가고 있으므로, 교육에서도 이용 가능한 것을 활용해야 합니다. In the following, I will explore the reasons why online education is a better choice.
First, online education (A)[breaks down / builds up] the barriers of time and space. Learners can access learning programs from anywhere and at any time. For instance, take Khan Academy, an online education program providing free lectures. It started when its founder, Sal Khan, uploaded teaching videos he made for his cousin who was living (B)[far away / nearby]. Now learners from all around the world can enjoy the program’s outstanding lectures on a wide variety of subjects at any time they want.
Second, online education caters to personalized learning opportunities that meet the various needs of each learner. One of the criticisms of traditional education is that it takes a one-size-fits-all approach that (C)[manages / fails] to address the various needs of students. In contrast, online learning can offer a customized learning path for each learner. To achieve this, a computer learning program first assesses each learner’s current level and weaknesses. Based on the assessment, each learner is offered personalized online lessons and more detailed explanations when necessary. This kind of personalized feedback process can be highly interactive and motivate learners to reach higher levels of achievement.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: breaks down / nearby / fails
builds up / far away / manages
breaks down / far away / fails
builds up / nearby / fails
breaks down / far away / manages
solution:
(A) 뒤에서 학습자들이 언제 어디서나 학습 프로그램에 접속할 수 있다고 했으므로 온라인 교육은 시간과 공간의 장벽을 없앤다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 breaks down(~을 무너뜨리다)이 적절하다.
build up ~을 강화하다, ~을 더 높이다
(B) 앞에서 학습자들이 언제 어디서나 학습 프로그램에 접속할 수 있으며, 뒤에서 전 세계의 학습자들이 원하는 시간에 언제든지 뛰어난 강의를 즐길 수 있다고 했으므로 Sal Khan이 멀리 살고 있는 사촌을 위해 강의 영상을 만들었다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 far away(멀리)가 적절하다.
nearby 가까이에
(C) 뒤에서 대조를 나타내는 In contrast(이에 반해)와 함께 온라인 학습은 각 학습자에게 맞춤형 학습 경로를 제공할 수 있다고 했으므로, 그와 반대로 전통적 교육은 학생들의 다양한 요구를 다루지 못한다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 fails(~하지 못하다)가 적절하다.
manage ~을 해내다

solution:
온라인 교육이 전통적인 교육보다 우수하다고 주장하며, 그 이유로 온라인 교육이 시간과 공간의 제약을 없애 학습자가 언제 어디서나 학습 프로그램에 접근할 수 있다는 점과 학습자의 수준과 약점을 평가하여 각자의 다양한 필요에 맞는 맞춤형 학습 과정과 수업을 제공할 수 있다고 설명하는 글이므로 이 글의 요지로 ⑤ ‘디지털 학습은 더 큰 유연성과 개별화된 수업을 가능하게 하기 때문에 전통적인 학교 교육보다 장점을 가진다.’가 적절하다.
